words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

words.ex: Some people follow that cult blindly.
words.ex_cn: 有些人盲目追随那个狂热崇拜。
words.en: A cult is a group of people who have extreme admiration for a particular person, idea, or thing, often following unusual or extreme practices or beliefs.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.ex: The farmer's cultivation of rice takes months.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植水稻需要几个月的时间。
words.en: The process of trying to acquire or develop a quality or skill.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

words.tr:
n. 未来；将来；前途；
adj. 将来的；未来的；
words.ex: We cannot predict the future.
words.ex_cn: 我们无法预测未来。
words.en: The future is the time after the present, or the events that will happen then.

words.ex: The car has a futuristic design.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车具有未来派的设计。
words.en: If you describe something as futuristic, you mean that it is very modern and unusual in appearance, and often looks as if it comes from a time in the future.

words.tr: n. 未来学家；未来主义者
words.ex: He is a futurist who predicts future technology.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位预测未来科技的未来学家。
words.en: A futurist is someone who studies and predicts what might happen in the future, especially in relation to a particular subject such as technology or society.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.ex: He showed maturity when he apologized for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他为自己的错误道歉时，表现出了成熟。
words.en: Maturity is the state of being fully developed or grown, or the time when a financial arrangement becomes ready to be paid.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.tr:
n. 狂喜；非常高兴
v. 使…狂喜
words.ex: She felt rapture when she saw the sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到日出时，感到无比欣喜。
words.en: A feeling of intense pleasure or joy.

words.tr: n. 目标；进球得分；球门；
words.ex: His goal is to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的目标是按时完成项目。
words.en: A goal is an aim or purpose that a person or a group of people is trying to achieve.

words.ex: He burns coal to keep his house warm.
words.ex_cn: 他烧煤来让房子暖和。
words.en: Coal is a hard black substance that is extracted from the ground and burned as fuel.

words.tr:
n. 外衣；大衣；
v. 覆盖；
words.ex: He put on his coat before going out.
words.ex_cn: 他出门前穿上了外衣。
words.en: A coat is a piece of clothing with long sleeves which you wear over your other clothes when you go outside.

words.ex: He wears a black overcoat in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天穿一件黑色大衣。
words.en: An overcoat is a long warm coat that you wear over your other clothes in cold weather.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.ex: He had a sore throat after singing all night.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一整晚后喉咙疼。
words.en: Your throat is the back part of your mouth, where it connects to your neck. It includes the passage that leads from your mouth to your stomach and lungs.

words.ex: The boat floats on the water.
words.ex_cn: 船在水面上浮动。
words.en: To float means to stay on the surface of a liquid and not sink, or to move slowly in the air or on water.

words.tr: adj. 漂浮的； v. “float”的现在分词；
words.ex: The floating leaves drifted on the lake.
words.ex_cn: 漂浮的叶子在湖面上飘荡。
words.en: Something that is floating is not fixed in one place or position but moves around or is easy to move.

words.tr:
adj. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
adv. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
words.ex: The boat stayed afloat during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船在风暴中保持漂浮。
words.en: If someone or something is afloat, they are floating on water or in the air.

words.ex: He lived in Paris for a decade.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎生活了十年。
words.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: He goes to a music academy every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末去音乐学院。
words.en: An academy is a type of school for special training or a society for the advancement of art, science, or literature.

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: He is an academician at the national academy.
words.ex_cn: 他是国家科学院的院士。
words.en: An academician is a member of an academy, especially of an academy of arts or sciences.

words.ex: He made a big effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他努力完成这个项目，按时交工。
words.en: If you make an effort to do something, you try hard to do it.

words.ex: The soldiers defended the fort during the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在战斗中保卫了堡垒。
words.en: A fort is a strong building or a place with a wall or fence around it where soldiers can stay and be safe from the enemy.

words.tr: v. 设防御工事；加强；增加营养物
words.ex: The soldiers fortify the hill with walls and trenches.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在山上用墙壁和战壕设防御工事。
words.en: To strengthen a place with defensive works so as to protect it against attack; to strengthen or invigorate someone mentally or physically.

words.tr: n. 堡垒；要塞；防御工事
words.ex: The castle has strong fortification against attacks.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡有坚固的防御工事来抵御攻击。
words.en: Fortification refers to the act of fortifying or the state of being fortified, especially in the context of military defense structures designed to protect a place against attack.

words.ex: The soft chair gives me comfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把软椅子给我带来舒服。
words.en: If you comfort someone, you make them feel less worried, unhappy, or upset, for example by saying kind things to them.

words.ex: This chair is very comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子非常舒适。
words.en: If a piece of furniture or an item of clothing is comfortable, it makes you feel physically relaxed when you use it or wear it, for example because it is soft.

words.ex: The hard chair caused him discomfort.
words.ex_cn: 这把硬椅子让他感到不舒适。
words.en: Discomfort is a feeling of slight pain or physical unease, or a feeling of worry or embarrassment.

words.ex: He lost his fortune in the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他在股市中失去了他的财产。
words.en: A large amount of money or assets; chance or luck as an external force in human affairs.

words.ex: He is fortunate to have a good job.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运拥有一份好工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

words.ex: Fortunately, the bus came just in time.
words.ex_cn: 幸运的是，公交车正好准时到了。
words.en: Used to say that something good has happened, especially when it could have been bad.

words.ex: It was unfortunate that he missed the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他没赶上公交车，真是不幸。
words.en: If you describe someone as unfortunate, you mean that something unpleasant or unlucky has happened to them. You can also describe the unpleasant things that happen to them as unfortunate.

words.ex: Unfortunately, he missed the bus.
words.ex_cn: 不幸的是，他错过了公交车。
words.en: Used to say that something is sad, disappointing, or has a bad effect.

words.tr:
v. 驾驶；驱使；
n. 动力；
words.ex: He drives a car to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: To operate and control the direction and speed of a motor vehicle; to push, propel, or carry along forcibly or strongly.

words.ex: The driver stopped the car at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 司机在红灯处停了车。
words.en: A driver is a person who drives a vehicle.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: The derivation of this word is from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的起源是拉丁语。
words.en: Derivation refers to the process by which a word is formed from another word or from a root, especially by the addition of an affix.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: The prisoners suffered from sleep deprivation.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们因睡眠剥夺而受苦。
words.en: Deprivation is the lack or denial of something considered to be a necessity.

words.ex: He strives to finish his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力完成作业。
words.en: If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.ex: He arrives at the station at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他早上8点到达车站。
words.en: To reach a place, especially at the end of a journey.

words.ex: The arrival of the train was delayed by 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 火车的到达晚了20分钟。
words.en: The act of coming to a place or the moment when something or someone arrives.

words.tr:
n. 竞争者；敌手；
v. 竞争；相匹敌；
words.ex: He is my main rival in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他是我在比赛中主要的竞争者。
words.en: A rival is a person, group, or organization that you are competing with in the same activity or the same area.

words.ex: The rivalry between the two teams is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍之间的竞争非常激烈。
words.en: Competition for the same objective or for superiority in the same field.

words.ex: His profession is a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的职业是教师。
words.en: A profession is a type of job that requires advanced education or training.

words.tr:
adj. 专业的；职业的；
n. 专业人士；
words.ex: He is a professional teacher with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的专业教师。
words.en: A professional is a person who has a job that requires special training and education, especially one that involves a high level of skill or knowledge.

words.ex: The professor teaches physics at the university.
words.ex_cn: 这位教授在大学教物理。
words.en: A professor is a senior teacher in a college or university.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: I occasionally walk my dog in the park.
words.ex_cn: 我偶尔在公园遛狗。
words.en: If something happens occasionally, it happens sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.tr:
n. 缺乏；短缺；
v. 缺乏；短缺；
words.ex: There is a lack of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: If there is a lack of something, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.ex: The rope is slack and hangs loosely.
words.ex_cn: 绳子是松弛的，垂挂着。
words.en: If something is slack, it is loose and not firmly stretched or tightly in position. It can also describe a period of low activity or a lack of effort in work or activity.

words.ex: I ate an apple as a snack after school.
words.ex_cn: 我放学后吃了一个苹果当小吃。
words.en: A snack is a small amount of food that is eaten between meals.

words.tr:
n. 一摞；一叠；一堆；大烟囱；
v. 把…放成整齐的一摞；
words.ex: He put the books in a stack on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把书堆成一摞放在桌子上。
words.en: A stack is a pile of things, usually arranged one on top of another.

words.tr:
n. 架子；支架；齿条；破坏
v. 折磨；使痛苦；放在架上；累计（得分）
words.ex: He put the books on the rack.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放在架子上。
words.en: A rack is a frame or shelf, usually with bars or hooks, that is used for holding things or for hanging things on. As a verb, to rack something means to cause great pain or suffering to someone.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.ex: My family follows the tradition of eating dumplings on New Year's Eve.
words.ex_cn: 我的家庭遵循除夕吃饺子的传统。
words.en: A tradition is a custom or belief that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people.

words.ex: He wears traditional clothes on holidays.
words.ex_cn: 他在节日时穿传统服装。
words.en: Traditional refers to customs, beliefs, or methods that have existed for a long time without changing.

words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: The invader came from a faraway land.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者来自一个遥远的地方。
words.en: An invader is someone who enters a place by force in order to conquer or occupy it.

words.ex: The invasive plant spreads quickly and kills other plants.
words.ex_cn: 这种侵入性植物生长迅速，会杀死其他植物。
words.en: If you describe something as invasive, you mean that it spreads very quickly and is difficult to stop.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: He tried evasion to avoid paying taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃避缴税。
words.en: The act of avoiding something that you are supposed to do or deal with.

words.tr:
adj. 南极的；
n. 南极地区；
words.ex: The antarctic ice is melting fast.
words.ex_cn: 南极的冰正在迅速融化。
words.en: The Antarctic is the area around the South Pole, characterized by its cold climate and ice-covered landscapes.

words.tr:
n. 北极地区；
adj. 北极的；
words.ex: Polar bears live in the arctic.
words.ex_cn: 北极熊生活在北极地区。
words.en: The Arctic is the area around the Earth's North Pole, characterized by cold temperatures and ice.

words.tr:
v. 成弧线；
n. 弧；弧形物；
words.ex: The rainbow arcs across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹在天空中形成一道弧线。
words.en: An arc is a smoothly curving line or movement.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.ex: My birthday is in March.
words.ex_cn: 我的生日在三月。
words.en: March is the third month of the Gregorian calendar, following February and preceding April.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.ex: He studies architecture at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学学习建筑学。
words.en: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical structures.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: The country still has a monarchy with a king as the head of state.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家仍然实行君主制，国王是国家元首。
words.en: A monarchy is a form of government in which a country is ruled by a monarch, such as a king or queen.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: The school has a hierarchical system.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个等级制度。
words.en: A hierarchical system or organization is one in which people have different ranks or positions, depending on how important they are.

words.ex: The ship dropped its anchor in the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船在港口放下了锚。
words.en: An anchor is a heavy object that is dropped from a boat or a ship into the water to prevent the vessel from moving.

words.ex: The ship stopped at the anchorage to wait for the tide.
words.ex_cn: 船在停泊处停靠，等待涨潮。
words.en: An anchorage is a place where boats or ships can anchor safely.

words.tr:
v. 集中；聚焦；
n. 中心点；焦点；
words.ex: He needs to focus on his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you focus on a particular topic or if your attention is focused on it, you concentrate on it and think about it, discuss it, or deal with it, rather than dealing with other topics.

words.ex: He learned about sex in biology class.
words.ex_cn: 他在生物课上学到了性。
words.en: Sex refers to the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences rather than biological ones.

words.ex: He wore a sexy shirt to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件性感的衬衫去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as sexy, you mean that it is attractive in a way that suggests sex or sexual activity.

words.ex: He learned about sexual health in school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习了性健康。
words.en: Relating to the instincts, physiological processes, and activities connected with physical attraction or intimate physical contact between individuals.

words.ex: The house has a small annex for storage.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个用于存放物品的小附属物。
words.en: To annex means to take control of a country, region, etc., especially by force; to add an area or region to a country, state, etc. : to take control of (a territory or place).

words.ex: The annexation of the small country by its neighbor caused international protest.
words.ex_cn: 邻国对这个小国的吞并引发了国际抗议。
words.en: The act of annexing, especially territory.

words.ex: The index of 2 in 2^3 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 2^3 中 2 的指数是 3。
words.en: An index is a system by which changes in the value of something and the rate at which it changes can be recorded, measured, or interpreted.

words.tr: adj. 某个；确定的；一定的；一定程度上的；
words.ex: I saw a certain man near the park.
words.ex_cn: 我在公园附近看到某个男人。
words.en: If you are certain about something, you have no doubt about it.

words.tr: adv. 毫无疑问地；确定地；当然；
words.ex: He will certainly come to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无疑问会来参加派对。
words.en: Without doubt; definitely.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.ex: He is uncertain about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个答案不确定。
words.en: If you are uncertain about something, you do not know what is true, what is going to happen, or what you should do.

words.ex: There is uncertainty about the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天的天气还不确定。
words.en: Uncertainty is a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain.

words.ex: We should talk about the plan for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们应该谈谈明天的计划。
words.en: To discuss or mention a particular subject.

words.tr: v. 说话；交谈；“talk”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is talking to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他正在和朋友说话。
words.en: The act of speaking or discussing something with someone.

words.ex: The captain sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 船长驾驶船穿越了海洋。
words.en: A captain is the person in charge of a ship or an aircraft, or a leader of a team or group.

words.ex: She pulled the curtain to block the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 她拉上帷幕以挡住阳光。
words.en: A curtain is a piece of material that hangs down, often used to cover a window or to divide a room.

words.tr: v. “be”的现在分词；是；在； n. 存在；生物；人；生命；
words.ex: He is being quiet in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他正在图书馆里保持安静。
words.en: The state or quality of having existence.

words.ex: Exercise helps with your well-being.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有助于你的健康。
words.en: The state of being comfortable, healthy, or happy.

words.ex: I used my card to pay for the groceries.
words.ex_cn: 我用我的银行卡支付了杂货费用。
words.en: A card is a piece of stiff paper or thin cardboard on which something is written or printed, or a small rectangular piece of plastic containing personal data in a machine-readable form.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr:
n. 需求；要求；
v. 要求；需求；
words.ex: The demand for clean water is increasing.
words.ex_cn: 对清洁水的需求正在增加。
words.en: If you demand something, you ask for it very forcefully, often because you think you have a right to do so.

words.tr: adj. 要求高的；费力的； v. 需要；“demand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The job is demanding because it needs long hours and high focus.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作要求高，因为它需要长时间工作和高度专注。
words.en: Requiring much effort or attention; exacting.

words.tr:
n. 指挥；命令；
v. 掌握；
words.ex: The general has command of the army.
words.ex_cn: 将军指挥着军队。
words.en: If someone in authority commands you to do something, they tell you that you must do it.

words.ex: The commander gave the order to advance.
words.ex_cn: 指挥官下达了前进的命令。
words.en: A commander is a person in authority, especially in the armed forces, who gives orders and is responsible for the actions of those under their command.

words.ex: Can you explain this math problem?
words.ex_cn: 你能解释一下这个数学问题吗？
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by describing or giving information about it.

words.ex: He gave a simple explanation for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的错误给出了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An explanation is a statement or account that makes something clear or provides a reason for something.

words.ex: The teacher gave an explanatory note to help students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个解释性的笔记来帮助学生。
words.en: Serving or intended to explain or make clear.

words.ex: He complains about the loud noise every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都抱怨噪音太大。
words.en: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or resentment, usually because of a particular situation or someone's actions.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: He felt great pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到极大的痛苦。
words.en: Pain is the feeling of great discomfort you have, for example when you have been hurt or when you are ill.

words.ex: The cut on his finger is painful.
words.ex_cn: 他手指上的伤口很疼。
words.en: If something is painful, it causes you a lot of physical or emotional pain.

words.tr:
n. 平原；
adj. 简单明了的；朴素的；
words.ex: The cows graze on the plain.
words.ex_cn: 牛在平原上吃草。
words.en: If something is plain, it is easy to see, hear, or understand.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.tr: adj. 流行的；受欢迎的；大众的；
words.ex: This song is popular among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中很流行。
words.en: liked, admired, or enjoyed by many people or by a particular person or group

words.ex: The popularity of this song grew quickly on social media.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在社交媒体上的流行迅速增长。
words.en: The state or condition of being liked, admired, or supported by many people.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.ex: I like fruits, particularly apples.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果。
words.en: Used to single out a subject to which a statement is especially applicable.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: She looked at herself in the mirror.
words.ex_cn: 她对着镜子看自己。
words.en: A mirror is a flat piece of glass which reflects light, so that when you look at it you can see yourself reflected in it.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr:
adj. 有规律的；经常的；常见的；
n. 常客；
words.ex: He goes for a run every morning, a regular habit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步，这是一个有规律的习惯。
words.en: Something that is regular happens or is done at equal intervals or is consistent in pattern or occurrence.

words.ex: The regularity of his daily routine helps him stay focused.
words.ex_cn: 他日常作息的规律性帮助他保持专注。
words.en: The quality or state of being regular; the condition of being governed by or according to rules, principles, or established customs.

words.ex: The shape has irregular sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个形状的边是不规则的。
words.en: Something that is irregular does not follow the expected pattern, plan, or method; it is not regular.

words.ex: He uses binoculars to watch birds in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他用望远镜在公园里看鸟。
words.en: Binoculars are an instrument that you hold up to your eyes to look at objects that are far away. It consists of two small telescopes joined together.

words.ex: He speaks English every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天讲英语。
words.en: To say words in order to express thoughts, feelings, or opinions.

words.ex: The speaker told a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 说话者讲了一个有趣的故事。
words.en: A speaker is someone who speaks, especially someone who gives a speech or makes a presentation.

words.ex: The spokesman spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokesman is a man who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization.

words.ex: The spokeswoman spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 女发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokeswoman is a woman who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization.

words.ex: The spokesperson spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokesperson is a person who speaks officially for a group or an organization.

words.ex: He gave a short speech at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上做了一个简短的讲话。
words.en: Speech is the expression of or the ability to express thoughts and feelings by articulate sounds.

words.tr: adj. 无言以对的；一时语塞的
words.ex: He was speechless when he saw the gift.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到礼物时，他哑口无言。
words.en: If you are speechless, you are temporarily unable to speak, usually because something has shocked or surprised you.

words.ex: Children tend to be more active in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子往往在早上更活跃。
words.en: If someone tends to do something, they usually do it or they often do it.

words.ex: There is a tendency for people to use phones before bed.
words.ex_cn: 人们在睡觉前使用手机是一种趋势。
words.en: A tendency is a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction, which is often bad or undesirable.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

words.ex: The trend shows more people are using electric cars.
words.ex_cn: 这个趋势表明越来越多的人在使用电动汽车。
words.en: A trend is a general development or change in a situation or in the way that people are behaving.

words.tr: v. 出席；参加；注意；照料；
words.ex: He will attend the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会出席会议。
words.en: To be present at an event, meeting, or function; to take care of or look after someone or something.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.ex: The child needs attention when he does homework.
words.ex_cn: 孩子做作业时需要被关注。
words.en: Attention is the act of focusing your mind on something and taking notice of it.

words.tr: adj. 注意的；专心的；留心的；关心的
words.ex: The child is attentive in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子上课很专心。
words.en: If you are attentive, you are paying close attention to what is being said or done.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.tr: adj. 延长的；扩大范围的；延伸的；
words.ex: The meeting was extended by thirty minutes.
words.ex_cn: 会议被延长了三十分钟。
words.en: Made larger or longer than usual.

words.ex: The extent of his knowledge surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识广度让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The area or length to which something extends.

words.ex: I intend to go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我打算明天去公园。
words.en: If you intend to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

words.ex: His intention was to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An intention is an idea or plan of what you are going to do.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.ex: He pretends to sleep when his mom asks him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他假装睡觉。
words.en: If you pretend that something is the case, you act in a way that is intended to make people believe that it is the case, although in fact it is not.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The superintendent of the school is very strict.
words.ex_cn: 学校的主管非常严格。
words.en: A superintendent is a person who is in charge of a particular department or activity, especially within a school, housing project, or police force.

words.ex: He adds two and three to get five.
words.ex_cn: 他把二和三相加得到五。
words.en: To put something together with something else so as to increase the size, number, or amount.

words.ex: The addition of a new chair made the room more comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 增加一把新椅子让房间更舒适了。
words.en: An addition is something that is added to something else, often to improve it or make it larger.

words.ex: He needs additional time to finish the homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要额外的时间来完成作业。
words.en: If something is additional, it is extra and is added to what is already there.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: He has an addiction to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏上瘾了。
words.en: Addiction is the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something as a habit, especially something harmful.

words.ex: The game is addictive and hard to stop playing.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏令人上瘾，很难停止玩。
words.en: If a substance or activity is addictive, it makes you want more of it so that you become dependent on it.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: The attraction of the city draws many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: An attraction is something that makes people want to go to a place or do a particular thing because they are interested in it.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr: n. 承包商；承包人；订约人
words.ex: The contractor fixed the roof last week.
words.ex_cn: 承包商上周修好了屋顶。
words.en: A contractor is a person or company that undertakes a contract to provide materials or labor to perform a service or do a job.

words.ex: The contraction of the muscle helps you move your arm.
words.ex_cn: 肌肉的收缩帮助你移动手臂。
words.en: A contraction is a process of becoming smaller or shorter, or a word that is made shorter by leaving out some letters.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.ex: The subtraction of 5 from 10 gives 5.
words.ex_cn: 10减去5等于5。
words.en: Subtraction is the process of taking one number or amount away from another.

words.ex: He must face his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: The front part of a person's head from the forehead to the chin, or the corresponding part in an animal.

words.ex: He has a facial scar from an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上有一道因事故留下的疤痕。
words.en: Facial means relating to the face or designed for use on the face.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.tr:
n. 表面；
v. 显露；
words.ex: The surface of the table is smooth.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的表面很光滑。
words.en: The outer or top part of something; to rise to the surface of water or to become known after being hidden or secret.

words.ex: He read the preface before starting the book.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始读这本书之前读了序言。
words.en: A preface is an introduction at the beginning of a book, which explains what the book is about or why it was written.

words.ex: The blacksmith heated the metal in the furnace.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠在熔炉里加热金属。
words.en: A furnace is a device that produces heat for warmth or to melt materials.

words.ex: In this village, it is a custom to light lanterns during the festival.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村庄，节日期间点灯笼是一种习俗。
words.en: A custom is an activity, a way of behaving, or an event which is usual or traditional in a particular society or in particular circumstances.

words.ex: The customer bought a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 这位客户买了一部新手机。
words.en: A customer is someone who buys goods or services from a shop or business.

words.ex: He accustoms himself to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己习惯早起。
words.en: If you accustom yourself or someone else to something, you make yourself or them familiar with it or used to it.

words.tr:
adj. 一些；某些；
pron. 有些；若干；
words.ex: I need some water.
words.ex_cn: 我需要一些水。
words.en: used to refer to an unspecified amount or number of something

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.ex: The mother won custody of her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲获得了孩子的监护权。
words.en: Custody is the legal right or duty to care for someone or something, especially a child after its parents have separated or died.

words.ex: We will discuss the homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天讨论作业。
words.en: To discuss something means to talk about it with someone and tell each other your ideas or opinions.

words.ex: We had a discussion about homework.
words.ex_cn: 我们进行了一次关于作业的讨论。
words.en: A discussion is a conversation or debate about a specific topic.

words.ex: The atom is the smallest part of matter.
words.ex_cn: 原子是物质的最小单位。
words.en: An atom is the smallest unit of ordinary matter that forms a chemical element. Every solid, liquid, gas, and plasma is composed of neutral or ionized atoms.

words.ex: The atomic structure of hydrogen is simple.
words.ex_cn: 氢的原子结构很简单。
words.en: relating to atoms or the energy that comes from splitting atoms

words.ex: The book fell to the bottom of the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书掉到了架子的底部。
words.en: The lowest part or edge of something, especially the part on which it rests or is supported.

words.ex: We will meet at the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将在公园见面。
words.en: To come into the presence of someone by chance or arrangement.

words.tr: n. 会议；会面； v. 遇见；见面；“meet”的现在分词；
words.ex: The meeting starts at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议上午九点开始。
words.en: A meeting is an event in which a group of people come together to discuss things or make decisions.

words.ex: He greet his friend with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着向朋友问好。
words.en: To greet someone means to say hello to them or to welcome them.

words.tr:
n. 问候；迎接；致意
v. 问候；打招呼；迎接；“greet”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave me a warm greeting.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我一个热情的问候。
words.en: A greeting is something friendly that you say or do when you meet someone.

words.ex: The navy launched a large fleet to protect the coast.
words.ex_cn: 海军派出了一支大型舰队来保护海岸。
words.en: A fleet is a group of ships or vehicles that are controlled by one company or organization and are used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He wrote his name on a sheet of paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在一张纸上写了名字。
words.en: A sheet is a large piece of thin cloth used on a bed to lie on or under. It can also refer to a flat, thin piece of material, such as paper, metal, or glass.

words.ex: He computes the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快算出总成本。
words.en: If you compute a total, amount, or result, you calculate it.

words.ex: He uses a computer to do his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他用计算机做作业。
words.en: A computer is an electronic machine that can store and deal with large amounts of information.

words.tr: v. 使计算机化；用计算机做
words.ex: The school will computerize its records next year.
words.ex_cn: 学校明年将把记录电脑化。
words.en: To computerize something means to use computers to control or operate it, or to change something so that it can be controlled or operated by computers.

words.ex: He did the computation by hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手算了这个计算。
words.en: Computation is the process of calculating something, especially using a computer.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 有声望的；声誉好的
words.ex: He works for a reputable company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家信誉良好的公司工作。
words.en: A reputable person or organization is considered to be good and trustworthy by most people.

words.ex: He has a good reputation for honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他以诚实著称。
words.en: The opinion that people have about someone or something because of what has happened in the past.

words.tr: phrase. 淡化；轻描淡写；降低…的重要性
words.ex: He tried to play down his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图淡化自己的错误。
words.en: To make something seem less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr: adj. 有争议的；可商榷的
words.ex: The result is disputable because the data is unclear.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果是有争议的，因为数据不清楚。
words.en: If you say that something is disputable, you mean that it is not certain or that people may not agree about it.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.tr:
n. 商店；店铺；仓库；储存；
v. 贮藏；存储；
words.ex: I bought milk at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店买了牛奶。
words.en: A store is a building or part of a building where things are sold. In British English, a store is a large shop that sells many different kinds of goods. In American English, a store is any kind of shop.

words.ex: The barn is used for storage of grain.
words.ex_cn: 这个谷仓用于粮食的贮存。
words.en: The act of storing something or the space where things are stored.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: The restoration of the old house took two years.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的修复花了两年时间。
words.en: The act of returning something to its original condition, or the state of being returned to its original condition.

words.ex: My throat is sore after singing.
words.ex_cn: 我唱歌后喉咙疼。
words.en: If part of your body is sore, it causes you pain and discomfort.

words.tr:
n. 分数；得分；总谱；乐谱；
v. 得分；
words.ex: He got a high score on the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中得了高分。
words.en: If you score a particular amount or number in a game or test, you achieve that amount or number.

words.tr:
v. 护送；护卫
n. 护送者；护卫队
words.ex: He will escort her to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他将陪她去参加派对。
words.en: An escort is a person or vehicle that accompanies another person or vehicle, especially in order to provide protection or show them the way.

words.ex: The children played on the shore of the lake.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在湖岸玩耍。
words.en: The land along the edge of a sea, lake, or other large body of water.

words.ex: The sailors swam ashore after the boat sank.
words.ex_cn: 船沉没后，水手们游到了岸上。
words.en: If someone or something comes ashore, they come from the sea onto the shore.

words.ex: The storm broke out at night.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨在夜间爆发了。
words.en: A storm is very bad weather, with heavy rain, strong winds, and often thunder and lightning.

words.ex: The stormy sea crashed against the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨的海浪拍打着岩石。
words.en: Characterized by strong winds and usually rain, thunder, lightning, or snow.

words.tr:
n. 发展；进步；提前；
adj. 预先的；在前的；
v. 前进；发展；提前；
words.ex: The advance of technology has changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展改变了我们的生活。
words.en: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help it to succeed.

words.tr: adj. 先进的；高级的； v. 提前；前进；“advance”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This school uses advanced technology in classrooms.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校在教室里使用先进的技术。
words.en: An advanced system, method, or design is modern and has been developed from an earlier version of the same thing.

words.ex: The advancement of technology helps people live better.
words.ex_cn: 技术的进步帮助人们生活得更好。
words.en: The process of promoting a cause or plan; the act of moving forward or making progress.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.ex: It is advantageous to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 早起是有利的。
words.en: If something is advantageous to you, it is likely to benefit you.

words.ex: The disadvantage of living far away is long commute time.
words.ex_cn: 住得远的劣势是通勤时间长。
words.en: A disadvantage is a factor which makes someone or something less useful, acceptable, or successful than other people or things.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: He went on an adventure in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 他去丛林里冒险。
words.en: An adventure is an exciting experience or undertaking that is typically bold, sometimes risky.

words.ex: The adventurer climbed the high mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 这位冒险家独自爬上了高山。
words.en: An adventurer is someone who enjoys or seeks adventure, especially someone who travels to unknown or dangerous places.

words.tr: adj. 有冒险精神的；敢于创新的；
words.ex: He is an adventurous boy who loves climbing mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢爬山的有冒险精神的男孩。
words.en: Willing to take risks or to try out new methods, ideas, or experiences.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.tr:
n. 一半；
adj. 一半的；
adv. 一半地；
words.ex: He ate half of the apple.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了苹果的一半。
words.en: One of two equal parts into which something is or can be divided.

words.ex: He spoke on behalf of his team.
words.ex_cn: 他代表他的团队发言。
words.en: If you do something on someone's behalf, you do it for that person as their representative.

words.ex: The child behaves well in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现得很好。
words.en: To behave means to act in a particular way, especially in a way that is good or correct.

words.ex: His behavior at the party was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.ex: His behavioral changes worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为变化让他的父母担心。
words.en: Relating to the way in which someone behaves.

words.ex: He will continue walking after the break.
words.ex_cn: 休息后他会继续走路。
words.en: If someone or something continues to do something, they keep doing it and do not stop.

words.ex: The continuation of the project depends on funding.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的继续取决于资金。
words.en: The act of continuing something or the state of being continued.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: There are many shops on this avenue.
words.ex_cn: 这条大街上有许多商店。
words.en: An avenue is a wide street or main thoroughfare, often lined with trees or other landscaping.

words.ex: He looked at the menu and chose pasta.
words.ex_cn: 他看了菜单，选择了意大利面。
words.en: A menu is a list of the food that is available at a restaurant or café.

words.tr: adv. 更确切地说；宁可；相当；
words.ex: I don't like coffee; rather, I prefer tea.
words.ex_cn: 我不喜欢咖啡；更确切地说，我更喜欢茶。
words.en: You use rather to indicate that something is true to a fairly great extent, especially when you are talking about something unpleasant or undesirable.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.ex: We work together every day.
words.ex_cn: 我们每天一起工作。
words.en: If people do something together, they do it with each other.

words.ex: There are altogether five apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上面总共有五个苹果。
words.en: Altogether is used to emphasize that something is completely the case or to indicate the total number or amount of something.

words.tr:
adv. 进一步；更远；此外；
adj. 更多的；附加的；
v. 促进；
words.ex: He explained the problem, and then gave further examples.
words.ex_cn: 他解释了这个问题，然后给出了进一步的例子。
words.en: to a greater degree or extent

words.ex: He likes reading, and furthermore, he writes stories too.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢阅读，而且他还写故事。
words.en: In addition to what has been said; moreover.

words.ex: The accident happened yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 事故昨天发生了。
words.en: If something happens, it occurs as a result of a situation or course of action.

words.tr: v. 贡献；促成；捐献；投稿；
words.ex: He contributes money to the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他向慈善机构捐款。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.ex: His contribution helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他的贡献帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: A contribution is a gift or payment to a common fund or collection, or the part played by a person or thing in bringing about a result or helping something to advance.

words.tr: n. 投稿人；贡献者；因素；
words.ex: He is a contributor to the local newspaper.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地报纸的投稿人。
words.en: A contributor is someone who gives something, such as money, time, or ideas, to help achieve or provide something.

words.ex: The teacher will distribute the books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将把书分发给学生。
words.en: If you distribute things, you hand them or deliver them to a number of people.

words.ex: The distribution of students in the class is even.
words.ex_cn: 班级里学生的分布是均匀的。
words.en: The process of giving out or spreading something, or the way in which something is spread or arranged over an area or among a group of people.

words.ex: The distributive property says 3 times (4 + 5) equals 3 times 4 plus 3 times 5.
words.ex_cn: 分配律说 3 乘以 (4 + 5) 等于 3 乘以 4 加上 3 乘以 5。
words.en: Relating to the way that something is shared out among a group or spread over an area.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: The accident is attributable to poor road conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故可归因于糟糕的路况。
words.en: Capable of being attributed to someone or something.

words.ex: The word 'red' is an attributive in 'red car'.
words.ex_cn: 在 'red car' 中，'red' 是一个限定词。
words.en: An attributive adjective is an adjective that is placed before the noun it modifies, without a linking verb.

words.ex: The tribune spoke for the common people in ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 护民官在古罗马为平民发声。
words.en: A tribune was an official in ancient Rome who was elected by the plebeians to protect their interests. In modern usage, it can also refer to a platform or forum for public speaking.

words.ex: The fact is that he was late.
words.ex_cn: 事实是他迟到了。
words.en: A fact is a piece of information that is known to be true.

words.tr: adj. 根据事实的；真实的；
words.ex: His report is factual and accurate.
words.ex_cn: 他的报告是基于事实且准确的。
words.en: If something is factual, it is based on facts or concerns facts.

words.tr:
n. 因素；要素；倍数；
v. 把…因素包括进去；
words.ex: Weather is a factor in the game's outcome.
words.ex_cn: 天气是比赛结果的一个因素。
words.en: A factor is one of the things that affects an event, decision, or situation.

words.tr: n. 派系；派系斗争；内讧
words.ex: The faction argued loudly about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别就新规定激烈争论。
words.en: A faction is a group of people within a larger group who have different opinions and beliefs from the rest of the group.

words.ex: A fraction of the students passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 只有一小部分学生通过了考试。
words.en: A fraction is a small part or amount of something.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.tr:
v. 获得；增加；
n. 增益；获得；
words.ex: He gained a new skill last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月获得了一项新技能。
words.en: To gain means to obtain something that is useful, that gives you an advantage, or that is in some way positive, especially over a period of time.

words.ex: I found a great bargain at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场上找到了一件便宜货。
words.en: A bargain is an agreement between two people or groups in which each promises to do something in exchange for something else. It can also refer to something bought or offered for sale much more cheaply than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The bike has a metal chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆自行车有一条金属链条。
words.en: A chain consists of connected links which are typically made of metal, used for fastening or securing something, or for transmitting mechanical power.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.ex: The brain controls our thoughts and movements.
words.ex_cn: 大脑控制我们的思想和行动。
words.en: The brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.ex: He fills the bottle with water.
words.ex_cn: 他把瓶子装满水。
words.en: To make or become full; to put something into a container or space so that it is completely or almost completely full.

words.tr: v. 填充；装满；充满；“fill”的现在分词； n. 填充；
words.ex: He is filling the bottle with water.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把水倒入瓶子中。
words.en: A filling is a small amount of metal or plastic that a dentist puts in a hole in a tooth to prevent further decay.

words.tr:
n. 寒冷；寒意；
v. 变冷；使冰冷；
words.ex: The chill of the morning made me wear a jacket.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的寒冷让我穿上了夹克。
words.en: A chill is a feeling of coldness, often accompanied by shivering. It can also refer to a feeling of fear or anxiety. As a verb, to chill means to make something cold, or to relax and take it easy.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；冷漠的；
words.ex: The morning air was chilly.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的空气很寒冷。
words.en: Something that is chilly is unpleasantly cold.

words.ex: I paid the electric bill yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天付了电费账单。
words.en: A bill is a statement of money owed for goods or services, a proposed law presented to a legislature for approval, a piece of paper money, or the beak of a bird.

words.ex: The children played on the green hill.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在绿色的丘陵上玩耍。
words.en: A hill is a piece of land that is higher than the land that surrounds it, but not as high as a mountain.

words.ex: The village is in a hilly area near the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于靠近山地的多小山地区。
words.en: A hilly area has a lot of hills.

words.ex: The old mill stands by the river.
words.ex_cn: 旧磨坊坐落在河边。
words.en: A mill is a building in which grain is crushed to make flour. It can also refer to a factory where certain materials are processed or manufactured.

words.ex: The score was nil at the end of the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束时分数为零。
words.en: Nothing or none; used to indicate the absence of something.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.tr: n. 惊险小说（或戏剧、电影）；
words.ex: He loves watching thriller movies at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢晚上看惊险电影。
words.en: A thriller is a book, film, or play that tells an exciting story about something such as criminal activities or spying.

words.tr:
auxv. 将会；愿意；
n. 意志；意愿；遗嘱；
words.ex: I will go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天会去公园。
words.en: The word 'will' can be used as a noun to refer to the faculty by which a person decides on and initiates action, or as a verb to indicate a desire or intention to do something.

words.tr: adj. 愿意的；乐意的； v. “will”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is willing to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If someone is willing to do something, they are happy to do it if it is needed.

words.ex: His willingness to help made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他乐于帮忙，让每个人都感到开心。
words.en: The quality or state of being prepared to do something; readiness.

words.ex: The workers used a drill to make holes in the rock.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用钻机在岩石上打孔。
words.en: A drill is a tool or machine that you use for making holes, or a method of teaching people something by making them repeat it many times.

words.tr:
n. 烤架；铁格子
v. 烧烤；拷问
words.ex: He cooked the burgers on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他用烤架烤了汉堡。
words.en: To cook food on a metal frame over a fire, or a metal frame used for cooking food in this way.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The climb was perilous in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 在暴风雨中，这次攀登非常危险。
words.en: Full of danger or risk.

words.ex: The old woman predict rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言明天会下雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.ex: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.

words.ex: The weather was predictable today, just like yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气和昨天一样，是可以预见的。
words.en: If you say that an event or a situation is predictable, you mean that it is obvious in advance that it will happen or what it will be like.

words.ex: The weather is unpredictable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

words.ex: Dark clouds are a predictor of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的预示物。
words.en: A predictor is someone or something that makes it possible for you to say what will happen or how someone will behave in the future.

words.ex: The model gives predictive results for next month's sales.
words.ex_cn: 这个模型提供了下个月销售额的预测结果。
words.en: If you use predictive to describe something, you mean that it is able to predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: The prosecutor read the indictment in court.
words.ex_cn: 检察官在法庭上宣读了起诉状。
words.en: An indictment is a formal accusation that someone has committed a crime.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: The teacher gave a dictation of five sentences.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了一次五句话的听写。
words.en: Dictation is the speaking or reading aloud of words for someone else to write down.

words.ex: The dictator ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A dictator is a ruler who has complete power in a country, especially when this power has been obtained by force and is used unfairly or cruelly.

words.ex: I looked up the word in a dictionary.
words.ex_cn: 我在词典里查了这个词。
words.en: A dictionary is a book in which the words of a language are listed alphabetically, together with their meanings, pronunciations, and other information.

words.ex: He works in a medical center.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家医疗中心工作。
words.en: Relating to the science or practice of medicine.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.ex: He wants to study medicine at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习医学。
words.en: Medicine is the science or practice of the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

words.ex: This plant has medicinal properties.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物具有药用价值。
words.en: Having healing properties; used in the treatment of disease.

words.ex: He won a gold medal in the Olympics.
words.ex_cn: 他在奥运会上赢得了一枚金牌。
words.en: A medal is a small metal disc which is given as an award for bravery or as a prize in a sporting event.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；认真的；严肃的；
words.ex: The accident caused a serious injury.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故造成了严重的伤害。
words.en: If you are serious about something, you are sincere about it and mean what you say.

words.ex: He watched the whole series of the show.
words.ex_cn: 他看完了这部剧的整个系列。
words.en: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other.

words.tr:
adj. 连续的；连环的
n. 连续剧；连载小说
words.ex: He watched the serial episodes every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上观看连续的剧集。
words.en: A serial is a story or play that is broadcast on television or radio in several parts at fixed times, or a story that is published in a magazine or newspaper in several parts.

words.ex: The bridge connects the two cities.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥连接了两座城市。
words.en: If something or someone connects one thing to another, or if one thing connects to another, the two things are joined together.

words.ex: The connection between the two wires is loose.
words.ex_cn: 两根电线之间的连接松了。
words.en: A connection is a relationship between two things, people, or groups.

words.ex: The phone has good connectivity in rural areas.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机在农村地区的网络连接很好。
words.en: Connectivity refers to the state or extent of being connected or interconnected, especially in the context of computer systems or networks.

words.ex: He disconnects the cable from the TV.
words.ex_cn: 他把电缆从电视上拔掉。
words.en: To disconnect something means to separate it from something else to which it is attached or connected.

words.tr: v. （使）相互连接；（使）互相联系
words.ex: The cities are interconnect by high-speed trains.
words.ex_cn: 这些城市通过高速列车相互连接。
words.en: To connect with each other.

words.ex: He collects stamps every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周收集邮票。
words.en: If you collect a number of things, you gather them together, usually because you want them for a particular purpose.

words.ex: His collection of old coins is very rare.
words.ex_cn: 他收集的旧硬币非常稀有。
words.en: A collection is a group of things, often of the same type, that have been gathered together over a period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr: adj. 有才智的；聪明的；明智的；
words.ex: The intelligent boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个有才智的男孩很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is intelligent has the ability to think, understand, and learn things quickly and well.

words.ex: He shows high intelligence in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题时表现出很高的智力。
words.en: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: He was neglectful of his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很疏忽。
words.en: If you describe someone as neglectful, you mean they fail to do everything they should do to look after someone or something properly.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.tr: n. 沉思；反射；反映；反省；
words.ex: He sat quietly in the garden for reflection.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐在花园里沉思。
words.en: A reflection is an image that you can see in a mirror, glass, or water.

words.ex: He became reflective after reading the old letter.
words.ex_cn: 他读完那封旧信后变得沉思起来。
words.en: If you are reflective, you are thinking deeply about something.

words.ex: He speaks a local dialect in his village.
words.ex_cn: 他在村子里说一种地方方言。
words.en: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.

words.ex: The weather varies from day to day.
words.ex_cn: 天气每天都在变化。
words.en: If things vary, they are different from each other in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The weather shows a lot of variation in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天天气变化很大。
words.en: A variation is a difference or change in the usual or expected amount, level, or form of something.

words.tr:
adj. 可变的；易变的；
n. 变量；
words.ex: The weather is variable in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天的天气是多变的。
words.en: A variable is something that is likely to vary; something that is subject to variation.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；不同的；各种的；
words.ex: He bought various fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

words.tr: n. （同一事物）不同种类；多样性；（动植物的）品种；变化；
words.ex: The store sells a variety of apples.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种各样的苹果。
words.en: If something has variety, it consists of things which are different from each other.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.ex: The file size is reduced by compression.
words.ex_cn: 通过压缩，文件大小被减小了。
words.en: Compression is the act or process of making something smaller or pressing it into a smaller space, or the state of being pressed or squeezed in this way.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.tr:
v. 表达；表示；
adj. 明确的；
n. 特快列车；快件服务；
words.ex: He can express his feelings clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的感受。
words.en: If you express an idea or feeling, or express yourself, you show what you think or feel.

words.ex: His expression showed he was happy.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情显示他很快乐。
words.en: The act of making your thoughts, feelings, etc., known by speech, writing, or some other method.

words.ex: Her expressive eyes showed all her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她富有表情的眼睛展现了她所有的感情。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as expressive, you mean that their behaviour clearly indicates their feelings or intentions.

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: His speech was very impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲非常令人印象深刻。
words.en: Something that is impressive makes you admire it because it is very good, large, important, etc.

words.ex: His smile left a good impression on me.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑给我留下了好印象。
words.en: An idea, feeling, or opinion about something or someone, especially one formed without conscious thought or on the basis of little evidence.

words.ex: He loves impressionism in painting.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢绘画中的印象派。
words.en: Impressionism is a style or movement in painting originating in France in the 1860s, characterized by a concern with depicting the visual impression of the moment, especially in terms of the shifting effect of light and color.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.tr: n. 压迫；压制；抑制；镇压
words.ex: The people suffered under oppression for years.
words.ex_cn: 人们多年来一直遭受压迫。
words.en: Oppression is the cruel or unfair treatment of a group of people.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；沉重的；难以忍受的；闷热的
words.ex: The oppressive heat made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人窒息的炎热让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people in an unfair and cruel way and prevent them from having opportunities and freedom.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.ex: He felt the repression of his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了压抑自己真实情感的痛苦。
words.en: Repression is the act of subduing someone or something by force, or the state of being subdued in such a way.

words.tr: adj. 镇压的；专制的；压抑的
words.ex: The government is repressive toward critics.
words.ex_cn: 政府对批评者实行压制。
words.en: If you describe a society, law, or system as repressive, you think that it treats people too harshly and severely, and often prevents them from expressing their opinions.

words.ex: He tried to suppress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: To suppress something means to prevent it from being expressed, known, or continuing.

words.ex: The government tried suppression of the protest.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图压制抗议。
words.en: The act of ending something by force or preventing it from being expressed or continuing.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: The new machine improves the efficiency of production.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器提高了生产的效率。
words.en: Efficiency is the ability to do something or produce something without wasting materials, time, or energy.

words.ex: The old machine is inefficient and uses too much energy.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器效率低，耗能太多。
words.en: If someone or something is inefficient, they do not use time, energy, or resources in the best way.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.ex: He has great proficiency in English.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: If you show proficiency in something, you show ability or skill at it.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们有足够的食物用于这次旅行。
words.en: If something is sufficient for a particular purpose, there is enough of it for the purpose.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.ex: His deficiency in math made him struggle in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的缺乏让他在课堂上很吃力。
words.en: A deficiency is a lack or shortage of something that is needed.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.tr:
n. 手；
v. 交；递；给；
words.ex: He waved his hand to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 他挥挥手打招呼。
words.en: The part of the body at the end of the arm that is used for holding, moving, touching, and feeling things.

words.ex: A handful of students stayed after class to ask questions.
words.ex_cn: 少数学生课后留下来提问。
words.en: A handful of something is a small amount of it, especially when it is not enough or when it is difficult to manage.

words.ex: A pocket calculator is handy for math problems.
words.ex_cn: 便携式计算器对于数学问题很方便。
words.en: If something is handy, it is useful and easy to use or to reach.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a handbook for the science project.
words.ex_cn: 老师给我们发了一本科学项目的手册。
words.en: A handbook is a type of reference work, or other collection of instructions, that is intended to provide ready reference.

words.tr:
n. 残疾；障碍；阻碍；不利
v. 妨碍；使不利
words.ex: He has a physical handicap but still runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有身体残疾，但仍然每天跑步。
words.en: A handicap is a condition that markedly restricts a person's ability to function physically, mentally, or socially.

words.tr:
adj. 有生理缺陷的；残疾的；弱智的
v. 妨碍；使不利；“handicap”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The school made the playground accessible for handicapped children.
words.ex_cn: 学校让操场方便残障儿童使用。
words.en: A handicapped person has a physical or mental disability.

words.ex: She sells handmade handicraft at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上出售手工制品。
