words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: His benevolence helped the poor family.
words.ex_cn: 他的仁慈帮助了这个贫困家庭。
words.en: The quality of being well meaning; kindness.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr:
adj. 固体的；坚固的；可靠的；
n. 固体；
words.ex: Ice is a solid form of water.
words.ex_cn: 冰是水的固体形式。
words.en: A solid substance or object stays the same shape whether it is in a container or not.

words.ex: The solidity of the bridge reassured the travelers.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥的可靠性让旅客们感到安心。
words.en: The state or quality of being solid; firmness and stability.

words.ex: The water will solidify when it gets very cold.
words.ex_cn: 水在非常冷的时候会变凝固。
words.en: If something solidifies or is solidified, it becomes solid or hard.

words.ex: The workers showed solidarity during the strike.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在罢工期间表现出团结。
words.en: Solidarity is unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest; mutual support within a group.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The company's consolidation improved its market position.
words.ex_cn: 公司的巩固增强了其市场地位。
words.en: The act of combining two or more things into a single more effective or coherent whole.

words.tr: adj. 独自的；单独的；孤寂的；
words.ex: He lives in a solitary house far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 他住在离城镇很远的独自一人的房子里。
words.en: A solitary person or thing is the only one in a place.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: His determination helped him finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他的决心帮助他完成了比赛。
words.en: Determination is the quality that you show when you have decided to do something and you will not let anything stop you.

words.tr: v. 决心；决定；“determine”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 坚决的；坚定的；有决心的；
words.ex: He is determined to finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他决心完成比赛。
words.en: If you are determined to do something, you have made a firm decision to do it and will not let anything stop you.

words.ex: The police will examine the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察将调查犯罪现场。
words.en: If you examine something, you look at it carefully.

words.ex: The doctor did an examination of his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生对他手臂进行了检查。
words.en: An examination is a formal test that you take to show your knowledge or ability in a particular subject, or to obtain a qualification.

words.ex: The examiner asked the student a difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 考官问了学生一个难题。
words.en: An examiner is a person who checks something carefully in order to see if it is correct or satisfactory, or who gives people a test to see what they know or can do.

words.ex: The examinee wrote his answers carefully.
words.ex_cn: 考生认真地写下了他的答案。
words.en: A person who is taking an examination.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.tr:
adj. 极度的；
n. 极端；极端的事物；
words.ex: He felt extreme pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到极度疼痛。
words.en: If you describe something as extreme, you mean that it is very great in degree or intensity.

words.ex: He felt pain in the extremity of his finger.
words.ex_cn: 他手指的末端感到疼痛。
words.en: An extremity is the furthest point or limit of something, or a situation of extreme difficulty or danger.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: The company will roll back the price increase.
words.ex_cn: 公司将撤销价格上调。
words.en: To return something to a previous state or condition, especially in computing or politics.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: He uses fertilizer to help his plants grow.
words.ex_cn: 他用肥料帮助植物生长。
words.en: A substance that is added to soil to improve the growth of plants.

words.ex: The doctor checked her fertility to help her get pregnant.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了她的生育力，以帮助她怀孕。
words.en: Fertility refers to the ability to produce offspring or to the quality of being fertile, especially in terms of soil or land.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: He saw the futility of trying to fix it himself.
words.ex_cn: 他看到了自己试图修理它的无用。
words.en: The quality of being futile or ineffective.

words.tr:
adj. 复杂的；
n. 综合楼（群）；
words.ex: The instructions are too complex for children.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明对孩子来说太复杂了。
words.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

words.ex: The problem has too much complexity.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题太复杂了。
words.en: Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.

words.tr: n. 肤色；面色；情况；局面
words.ex: Her complexion is very fair.
words.ex_cn: 她的肤色非常白皙。
words.en: The natural color, texture, and appearance of a person's skin, especially of the face.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.ex: The injury led to a complication in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他的康复过程复杂化了。
words.en: A complication is a problem or difficulty that makes a situation harder to deal with.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.ex: The math problem caused perplexity in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题让全班都感到困惑。
words.en: A state of confusion or uncertainty.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: His superiority in math helped him win the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的优越让他赢得了比赛。
words.en: If one side in a war or conflict has superiority, it has an advantage over its enemy, for example because it has more soldiers or better equipment.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: He felt inferiority when he compared himself to his smarter brother.
words.ex_cn: 当他把自己和更聪明的哥哥比较时，他感到自己处于劣势。
words.en: The state of being lower in status or quality than another or others.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.tr:
adj. （职位或等级）较低的；年幼的；（高中、大学的）三年级学生；
n. 年幼者；
words.ex: He is a junior employee in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是公司里职位较低的员工。
words.en: A junior person is younger or has a lower position than another person.

words.tr:
adj. 资深的；高级的；年长的；
n. 年长者；大四学生；
words.ex: He is a senior engineer with 20 years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有20年经验的资深工程师。
words.en: Higher in rank, status, or importance; older in age.

words.ex: He got the promotion because of his seniority.
words.ex_cn: 他因为资历深而获得了晋升。
words.en: Seniority is the state of being older or higher in rank than someone else.

words.ex: Prior to the meeting, we reviewed the report.
words.ex_cn: 在会议之前，我们复习了报告。
words.en: Existing or coming before in time, order, or importance.

words.ex: We need to prioritize tasks by their deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要根据截止日期给任务排出先后顺序。
words.en: To prioritize means to arrange or deal with in order of importance so that the most important thing is done or dealt with first.

words.tr: n. 需优先考虑的事；优先权；
words.ex: Homework is my top priority.
words.ex_cn: 作业是我最需要优先考虑的事。
words.en: If something is a priority, it is the most important thing you have to do or deal with, or must be done or dealt with before everything else you have to do.

words.tr:
v. 努力；斗争；挣扎；
n. 努力；斗争；难事；
words.ex: He struggles to finish his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都努力完成作业。
words.en: If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though it is difficult or other people are making it difficult for you.

words.ex: He tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
words.ex_cn: 他试图走私香烟过境。
words.en: To smuggle goods or people means to move them into or out of a country illegally.

words.tr: n. 走私（罪）； v. “smuggle”的现在分词；
words.ex: Smuggling drugs is a serious crime.
words.ex_cn: 走私毒品是一种严重的犯罪。
words.en: The illegal movement of goods into or out of a country.

words.ex: The smuggler carried drugs across the border.
words.ex_cn: 走私者把毒品带过了边境。
words.en: A smuggler is a person who smuggles goods.

words.ex: He tried to strangle his enemy with a rope.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用绳子勒死他的敌人。
words.en: To strangle someone means to kill them by squeezing their throat tightly so that they cannot breathe.

words.ex: The lion lives in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 狮子生活在丛林中。
words.en: A jungle is a dense, tropical forest that is home to a wide variety of plants and animals.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.ex: He found a new method to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: A method is a particular way of doing something.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.ex: The study uses a new methodology to collect data.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究使用了一种新的方法论来收集数据。
words.en: A methodology is a system of methods and principles for doing something, for example for teaching or for carrying out research.

words.ex: He bought a new device to take photos.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一个新设备来拍照。
words.en: A device is an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: He did revision for his math test last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚为数学考试进行了复习。
words.en: The act or process of revising; a revised or new version, as of a book or other written material.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.ex: The supervisor checked the workers' progress.
words.ex_cn: 主管检查了工人们的进展。
words.en: A supervisor is a person who oversees and directs the work of others.

words.ex: The teacher gave supervision to the students during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试期间监督学生。
words.en: The act of overseeing or directing a project, activity, or person.

words.tr: adj. 充满智慧的；明智的；英明的；
words.ex: The wise old man gave good advice.
words.ex_cn: 这位充满智慧的老人给出了很好的建议。
words.en: If you describe someone as wise, you mean that they have experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

words.ex: His wisdom helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的智慧帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: Wisdom is the ability to use your knowledge and experience to make good decisions and judgments.

words.ex: He visits the website every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天访问这个网站。
words.en: A website is a set of related web pages located under a single domain name, typically produced by a single person or organization.

words.ex: The site of the old church is now a park.
words.ex_cn: 旧教堂的位置现在是一个公园。
words.en: A site is a piece of ground that is used for a particular purpose or where a particular thing happens.

words.tr: adj. 装置外的；厂区外的；异地的; adv. 装置外；厂区外；异地地
words.ex: The company held an offsite meeting to brainstorm new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 公司举行了一次异地会议来集思广益新想法。
words.en: An offsite activity or event takes place away from the main place where people work or live.

words.tr: n. 寄生虫；寄生生物；依赖他人过活者；
words.ex: The parasite lives inside the host's body.
words.ex_cn: 这种寄生虫生活在宿主的体内。
words.en: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host organism and gets its food from or at the expense of its host.

words.ex: He sits on the bench every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上坐在长椅上。
words.en: If you are sitting somewhere, for example in a chair, your bottom is resting on the chair and the upper part of your body is upright.

words.tr: v. 坐；“sit”的现在分词； n. 坐着活动的一段时间；一次用餐时间；
words.ex: He is sitting on a chair.
words.ex_cn: 他正坐在椅子上。
words.en: The act of being in a seated position.

words.ex: The upper shelf is too high to reach.
words.ex_cn: 上面的架子太高了，够不着。
words.en: Higher in place or position; situated above another part.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；大量的；辽阔的；
words.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠巨大而空旷。
words.en: If you describe something as vast, you mean that it is very large.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The earthquake caused total devastation in the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震给这座城市造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: The state of being devastated; severe and widespread destruction or damage.

words.tr: adj. 毁灭性的； v. “devastate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The earthquake caused devastating damage to the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震对这座城市造成了毁灭性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as devastating, you are emphasizing that it is very harmful or damaging.

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.ex: The lock uses a simple combination of three numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁使用三个数字的简单组合。
words.en: A combination is a mixture of things or people that are combined.

words.tr: adj. 组合的；结合的； v. 组合；结合；“combine”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The combined effort of both teams won the game.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队的联合努力赢得了比赛。
words.en: Made by joining two or more things or people together.

words.ex: He bind the books with string.
words.ex_cn: 他用绳子把书捆起来。
words.en: To tie something or someone tightly or to fasten something.

words.tr: adj. 有法律约束力的；必须遵守的； n. 封皮； v. “bind”的现在分词；
words.ex: The contract is binding for both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同对双方都有法律约束力。
words.en: Binding refers to the act of fastening or securing something, or the material used to do this. It can also describe something that is obligatory or that imposes a legal or moral obligation.

words.ex: The blind man walks with a white cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位失明的男人用白色手杖走路。
words.en: Unable to see; lacking the sense of sight.

words.tr: phrase. 死胡同；没有出路的情况；无法继续发展的局面
words.ex: The road is a dead end.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是死胡同。
words.en: A dead end is a street or passage that is closed at one end, or a situation from which no progress can be made.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: He emphasizes the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 他强调作业的重要性。
words.en: To give special importance or prominence to (something) in speaking or writing.

words.tr: adj. 强调的；明确表示的；加强语气的
words.ex: He gave an emphatic no to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坚决的否定。
words.en: An emphatic statement or response is expressed in a very forceful and clear way.

words.ex: She showed empathy when her friend cried.
words.ex_cn: 当她的朋友哭泣时，她表现出了同感。
words.en: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: I sympathize with people who are hungry.
words.ex_cn: 我同情那些挨饿的人。
words.en: If you sympathize with someone who is in a bad situation, you feel sorry for them.

words.ex: She was sympathetic to his problems.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的问题很同情。
words.en: If you are sympathetic to someone who is in a bad situation, you are kind to them and show that you understand their feelings.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.tr:
adj. 审美的；美学的
n. 美学
words.ex: She loves the esthetic of old paintings.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢旧画的美感。
words.en: Relating to the appreciation of beauty or good taste, especially in the arts.

words.tr: v. 运转；操作；施行手术；
words.ex: The machine operates smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器运转顺畅。
words.en: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.ex: The operational system runs smoothly every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个运作系统每天运行顺畅。
words.en: If a system or service is operational, it is working or able to be used.

words.ex: The operator answered the phone quickly.
words.ex_cn: 接线员迅速接听了电话。
words.en: An operator is a person who operates equipment or a machine, or a person who is in charge of a telephone switchboard.

words.tr:
adj. 起作用的；运作中的
n. 技工；密探；特工
words.ex: The operative plan is to start tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实施的计划是明天开始。
words.en: An operative system or plan is one that is in use or being used. An operative is someone who works for a government agency or a private company, often doing secret or confidential work.

words.ex: They cooperate to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作以按时完成项目。
words.en: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The two companies showed good cooperation on the project.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司在这个项目上表现出良好的合作。
words.en: Cooperation is the process of working or acting together, which can be seen in many aspects of life, including business, science, and social interactions.

words.tr:
adj. 合作的；
n. 合作社；
words.ex: The two companies made a cooperative effort to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司合作努力解决问题。
words.en: A cooperative is an organization or business that is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The incorporation of new ideas improved the plan.
words.ex_cn: 新想法的结合改进了这个计划。
words.en: Incorporation is the process or result of forming a legal corporation, or the inclusion of something as part of a whole.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

words.ex: The separation of the two chemicals caused a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质的分离引起了反应。
words.en: The act of separating or the state of being separated.

words.tr:
n. 分离主义者；独立主义者
adj. 分裂主义的；独立主义的
words.ex: The separatist group wants to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个分离主义团体希望脱离这个国家。
words.en: A separatist is a person who supports the separation of a particular group of people from a larger body on the basis of ethnicity, religion, or gender.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: The sponge reached saturation and could not hold more water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵达到饱和，再也吸不下更多水了。
words.en: Saturation is the state or process that occurs when no more of something can be absorbed, combined with, or added.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；问题；困难；
v. 费神；
words.ex: He got into trouble for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规则而惹上了麻烦。
words.en: If you say that someone is in trouble, you mean that they are in a situation that is difficult to deal with and that may cause them problems.

words.tr: adj. 令人烦恼的；讨厌的；
words.ex: The noisy neighbors are troublesome.
words.ex_cn: 那些吵闹的邻居令人烦恼。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as troublesome, you mean that they cause you a lot of problems or worries.

words.tr:
adj. 高尚的；
n. 贵族；
words.ex: He made a noble decision to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个高尚的决定去帮助穷人。
words.en: If you say that someone is a noble person, you admire and respect them because they are unselfish and morally good.

words.ex: The nobility lived in large castles and owned much land.
words.ex_cn: 贵族住在大城堡里，拥有大量土地。
words.en: The quality of being noble in character, mind, birth, or rank.

words.ex: The child blew a bubble with gum.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用口香糖吹了一个气泡。
words.en: A bubble is a small ball of air or gas in a liquid, or a ball of air inside a solid substance such as glass.

words.ex: He writes a blog about travel.
words.ex_cn: 他写一个关于旅行的博客。
words.en: A blog is a website containing a writer's or group of writers' own experiences, observations, opinions, etc., and often having images and links to other websites.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.tr:
n. 原木；航海日志；
v. （正式地）记载；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly with a large log.
words.ex_cn: 大火用一根大原木烧得很旺。
words.en: A log is a piece of a thick branch or trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things. A log is also a written record of events, often on a ship or aircraft.

words.ex: The city has heavy smog in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市冬天有严重的雾霾。
words.en: Smog is a mixture of smoke and fog, or a similar mixture of air pollutants, which can be harmful to health.

words.ex: The sky was smoggy in the city.
words.ex_cn: 城市里的天空很雾霾。
words.en: If the weather is smoggy, there is a lot of smog in the air.

words.ex: He jogs every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上慢跑以保持健康。
words.en: To run at a slow, steady pace, especially as a form of exercise.

words.ex: The jogger was wearing bright colors to be more visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 这位慢跑者穿着亮色衣服，以便在夜间更加显眼。
words.en: A jogger is someone who runs at a slow, steady pace as a form of exercise.

words.ex: Nike is a famous brand.
words.ex_cn: 耐克是一个著名品牌。
words.en: A brand is a name, term, design, symbol, or any other feature that identifies one seller's good or service as distinct from those of other sellers.

words.tr: n. 品牌营销；品牌化； v. “brand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company spent money on branding to attract more customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司花钱做品牌营销以吸引更多的顾客。
words.en: The process of creating a unique name and image for a product in the consumers' mind, mainly through advertising campaigns with a consistent theme.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr:
v. 使滞留；使搁浅；
n. 方面；
words.ex: The storm stranded the travelers on the island.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使旅行者滞留在岛上。
words.en: If someone is stranded, they are left in a place that is difficult for them to get away from. A strand of something such as hair, wire, or thread is a single thin piece of it.

words.tr: adj. 搁浅的；处于困境的； v. 使搁浅；“strand”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The boat was stranded on the sandbank.
words.ex_cn: 船搁浅在沙洲上。
words.en: Left in a difficult or helpless situation, especially without means of escape or assistance.

words.ex: He went on an errand to buy milk.
words.ex_cn: 他去买牛奶了。
words.en: An errand is a short journey that you make in order to do a job for someone, for example when you go to a shop to buy something for them.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.ex: He showed great spirit when he tried again after failing.
words.ex_cn: 他在失败后再次尝试时展现了极大的精神。
words.en: The part of a person that includes their mind, feelings, and character rather than their body.

words.ex: He finds peace through spiritual meditation.
words.ex_cn: 他通过精神上的冥想找到平静。
words.en: Relating to the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.tr:
v. 喷吐；吐痰；吐口水
n. 唾沫；一块陆地；烤肉叉
words.ex: He likes to spit watermelon seeds.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢吐西瓜籽。
words.en: To spit means to force out the contents of the mouth, especially saliva, through the lips. It can also refer to the act of ejecting saliva or phlegm from the mouth, often as a gesture of contempt or disrespect.

words.tr:
v. 分开；分裂；
n. 划分；分歧；
words.ex: The tree split in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树在风暴中裂开了。
words.en: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.

words.ex: The dog fell into a deep pit.
words.ex_cn: 狗掉进了一个深坑。
words.en: A pit is a large hole in the ground, either natural or as a result of digging. It can also refer to a hollow or indentation in a surface, or a place where something is extracted, such as a mine. As a verb, to pit means to set someone or something in competition or to make a hollow or indentation in a surface.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；舞台；
v. 举行；上演；
words.ex: This is a critical stage in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这是他康复过程中的一个关键阶段。
words.en: A stage is a raised area in a theatre or hall where performers, speakers, or entertainers stand. It can also refer to a particular point or period in the development or progress of something.

words.ex: He staggered home after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了后摇摇晃晃地走回家。
words.en: If you stagger, you walk very unsteadily, as if you are about to fall.

words.tr: adj. 令人惊愕的； v. “stagger”的现在分词；
words.ex: The staggering cost of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目令人惊愕的费用让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Something that is staggering is very surprising and shocking.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.tr: n. 停滞；滞止；萧条；迟钝
words.ex: The economy is in stagnation.
words.ex_cn: 经济处于停滞状态。
words.en: A situation in which there is no progress or development.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.tr: n. 音乐会；演奏会；一致；和谐；
words.ex: We went to a concert last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去听了音乐会。
words.en: A concert is a performance of music by one or more musicians or singers, which usually takes place in the evening.

words.ex: They made a concerted effort to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同努力清理了公园。
words.en: A concerted action or effort is done by several people or groups working together.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: His assertion was simple: the project will finish on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的断言很简单：项目会按时完成。
words.en: A statement that is made with confidence but without proof.

words.ex: She is assertive when she speaks up for her rights.
words.ex_cn: 当她为自己权利发声时，表现得坚定自信。
words.en: Someone who is assertive behaves confidently and is not frightened to say what they want or believe.

words.ex: The camel walks across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼穿越沙漠。
words.en: A desert is a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand. If you desert someone or something, you leave them and no longer help or support them.

words.ex: Overgrazing causes desertification in dry areas.
words.ex_cn: 过度放牧会导致干旱地区的沙漠化。
words.en: Desertification is the process by which fertile land becomes desert, typically as a result of drought, deforestation, or inappropriate agriculture.

words.ex: He ate ice cream for dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他吃冰淇淋当甜食。
words.en: Dessert is a sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.ex: The insertion of the new paragraph made the text clearer.
words.ex_cn: 插入新段落使文本更清晰。
words.en: The act of putting something inside something else, or the thing that is put inside.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: He felt tired after the exertion of running up the hill.
words.ex_cn: 在努力跑上山后，他感到很累。
words.en: The use of physical or mental energy; hard work.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.tr:
n. 捆；束；包
v. 匆匆送走
words.ex: He bought a bundle of newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一捆报纸。
words.en: A bundle is a number of things that are tied or wrapped together so that they can be carried or stored easily.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: There is an abundance of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常丰富。
words.en: A very large quantity of something.

words.tr: n. 过错；故障；缺陷；断层；
words.ex: It was his fault that the car crashed.
words.ex_cn: 汽车撞车是他的过错。
words.en: A fault is a mistake or a weakness in something or someone.

words.tr: adj. 有缺陷的；有故障的；有错误的；
words.ex: The faulty phone keeps turning off.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺陷的手机总是自动关机。
words.en: If you describe something as faulty, you mean that it is not perfect or it has some weaknesses.

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.tr: phrase. 反面；另一面（常指事物的对立或不同方面）
words.ex: The flip side of being a celebrity is the constant media attention.
words.ex_cn: 成为名人的反面是持续不断的媒体关注。
words.en: The flip side refers to the opposite or less favorable aspect of a situation or argument.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: He gave a citation from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他引用了这本书中的一段话。
words.en: A citation is a reference to a published or unpublished source (not always the original source). More precisely, a citation is an abbreviated alphanumeric expression embedded in the body of an intellectual work that denotes an entry in the bibliographic references section of the work for the purpose of acknowledging the relevance of the works of others to the topic of discussion at the spot where the citation appears.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

words.tr: n. 朗诵；朗读；背诵；逐个叙述
words.ex: The boy did a recitation of the poem in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上背诵了这首诗。
words.en: A recitation is the act of saying a piece of poetry or literature that you have learned to an audience.

words.ex: He goes to the library every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午去图书馆。
words.en: A library is a building where books, documents, CDs, and sometimes videos and music are kept for people to read, study, or borrow.

words.ex: The librarian helps students find books.
words.ex_cn: 图书管理员帮助学生找书。
words.en: A librarian is a person who is in charge of a library or who has been trained to do this work.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；自由主义的；
n. 自由党党员；
words.ex: He is a liberal teacher who listens to students.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，会倾听学生的声音。
words.en: A liberal person, system, or policy is one that is in favour of allowing people a lot of freedom in their behaviour or opinions.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.ex: The liberation of the city ended the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的解放结束了战争。
words.en: Liberation refers to the act of setting someone free from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression; release.

words.ex: The address is 720 liberty street.
words.ex_cn: 地址是自由大街720号。
words.en: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions imposed by authority on one's way of life, behavior, or political views.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: He made his decision after long deliberation.
words.ex_cn: 他在深思熟虑后做出了决定。
words.en: Deliberation is the long and careful consideration of a subject.

words.tr:
adj. 额外的；
n. 额外的事物；
adv. 额外地；
words.ex: He did extra work to earn more money.
words.ex_cn: 他做了额外的工作来赚更多的钱。
words.en: If something is extra, it is added to an existing amount or number.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: The countries formed a federation to share resources.
words.ex_cn: 这些国家组成了一个联盟来共享资源。
words.en: A federation is a group of states or organizations that have joined together to form a single entity with a central government or authority.

words.ex: The two countries formed a confederate alliance to defend their borders.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家结成了同盟联盟以保卫它们的边界。
words.en: A confederate is someone who works with others to achieve a common goal, often in a political or military context. It can also refer to a member of a confederation, which is a union of states or groups united for a common purpose.

words.ex: The states formed a confederation to share power.
words.ex_cn: 这些州组成了一个联盟来分享权力。
words.en: A confederation is an organization which consists of a number of parties or groups united in an alliance.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；伟大的；
n. 巨人；伟人；
words.ex: The giant elephant stood near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的大象站在树旁。
words.en: A giant is an imaginary person who is very big and strong, especially one mentioned in old stories. In everyday language, a giant can also refer to a very large and successful company or organization.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.ex: His ignorance of the rules caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的无知导致了这个错误。
words.en: Lack of knowledge or information.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: The car won't start because the ignition is broken.
words.ex_cn: 汽车无法启动，因为点火器坏了。
words.en: The process of starting the combustion of fuel in an engine.

words.tr: adj. 即刻的；立即的；紧接的；最近的；
words.ex: He needs immediate help.
words.ex_cn: 他需要即刻的帮助。
words.en: An immediate action, event, or situation happens or exists without any delay.

words.tr:
n. 节目；程序；
v. 编程；
words.ex: We watched a funny program on TV last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在电视上看了一个有趣的节目。
words.en: A program is a set of instructions that a computer follows in order to perform a particular task.

words.ex: He left the room immediately after the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 铃声一响，他就立即离开了房间。
words.en: If something happens immediately, it happens without any delay.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
words.en: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link between people or groups in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The mediator helped the two sides reach an agreement.
words.ex_cn: 调解人帮助双方达成了协议。
words.en: A mediator is a person who tries to end a disagreement by helping the two sides to talk about and agree on a solution.

words.ex: They used mediation to solve their argument.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过调解解决了争端。
words.en: Mediation is a process in which a neutral third party helps two or more parties in a dispute to reach a mutually acceptable agreement.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.ex: He does meditation every morning to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以放松。
words.en: Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He felt intimidation when the teacher shouted at him.
words.ex_cn: 当老师对他大喊时，他感到害怕。
words.en: Intimidation is the act of making someone feel frightened or threatened, especially in order to make them do something.

words.tr: adj. 令人紧张不安的；令人胆怯的；
words.ex: The big dog looked intimidating to the small child.
words.ex_cn: 那只大狗看起来让小孩子感到紧张不安。
words.en: Something that is intimidating makes you feel nervous and frightened because it is very difficult, dangerous, or extreme.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.ex: His naivety made him trust strangers easily.
words.ex_cn: 他的天真使他很容易相信陌生人。
words.en: Naivety is the quality of being naive; innocence or lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment.

words.ex: He joined the navy after high school.
words.ex_cn: 他高中毕业后加入了海军。
words.en: The navy is the part of a country's armed forces that is trained to operate at sea.

words.ex: He works on a naval ship.
words.ex_cn: 他在一艘军舰上工作。
words.en: Naval means relating to the navy, especially to ships that are used in war.

words.ex: The cat occupies the sofa all day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫整天占据着沙发。
words.en: If people or things occupy a place, they are in it or fill it.

words.tr: v. 占据；占领；“occupy”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有人使用（或居住）；忙于；被占领的；
words.ex: The big tree occupies most of the yard.
words.ex_cn: 这棵大树占据了院子的大部分地方。
words.en: If a place or a building is occupied, someone is living or staying there.

words.ex: The occupancy of the hotel is high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天酒店的占用率很高。
words.en: The act of occupying or the state of being occupied, especially the condition of being occupied by tenants or the period during which a property is occupied.

words.ex: The occupant of the room is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的住户正在睡觉。
words.en: An occupant is someone who lives in or uses a particular room, building, or area of land.

words.tr: v. 先占；使全神贯注；占据…的思想
words.ex: The old man preoccupies the best seat in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人先占了公园里最好的座位。
words.en: If something is preoccupying you, you are thinking about it a lot or it is occupying your attention.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的； v. “preoccupy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was preoccupied with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他全神贯注于他的作业。
words.en: If you are preoccupied, you are thinking a lot about something or someone, and so you hardly notice other things.

words.ex: The occupation of the city by foreign troops lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 外国军队对这座城市的占领持续了多年。
words.en: An occupation is a job or profession, or a way of spending your time.

words.ex: He chose an occupational therapy course.
words.ex_cn: 他选择了一门职业治疗课程。
words.en: Relating to a job or profession.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.ex: His persuasion helped me change my mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的说服让我改变了主意。
words.en: Persuasion is the act of persuading someone to do something or to believe that something is true.

words.ex: His speech was persuasive and made everyone agree.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲很有说服力，让所有人都同意了。
words.en: A persuasive argument or reason is one that makes you believe that something is true or right.

words.tr: adj. 新鲜的；新的；刚发生的；
words.ex: She bought fresh apples from the market.
words.ex_cn: 她从市场买了新鲜的苹果。
words.en: Fresh food has been picked or produced recently, and has not been preserved, for example by being frozen or put in a tin.

words.tr: v. 使恢复精力；使复原；使变新
words.ex: A short nap can refresh you.
words.ex_cn: 小睡一会儿能让你恢复精力。
words.en: To refresh someone means to make them feel less tired or less hot.

words.tr: adj. 使人精神焕发的； v. “refresh”的现在分词；
words.ex: The cool breeze was refreshing after the hot walk.
words.ex_cn: 在炎热的散步之后，凉爽的微风使人精神焕发。
words.en: Something that is refreshing is pleasantly different and interesting.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.ex: He bought a ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一张电影票。
words.en: A ticket is a small, official piece of paper or card which shows that you have paid to enter a place such as a theatre or a sports ground, or shows that you have paid for a journey.

words.ex: He kick the ball into the goal.
words.ex_cn: 他把球踢进了球门。
words.en: To strike or propel with the foot; a blow or thrust delivered by the foot.

words.tr:
v. 点击；
n. 咔哒声；
words.ex: Click the button to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 点击按钮开始游戏。
words.en: To make a short, sharp sound, or to press a button on a computer mouse or other device to select something on a screen.

words.ex: I pick the red shirt for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我为派对选择红色衬衫。
words.en: To choose something from a group of things or people, or to remove something from a place using your fingers or a tool.

words.tr: adj. 挑剔的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is picky about his food.
words.ex_cn: 他对食物很挑剔。
words.en: Someone who is picky is very careful about choosing only what they like.

words.ex: He is sick and cannot go to school.
words.ex_cn: 他生病了，不能去上学。
words.en: If you are sick, you are ill. Sick can also mean feeling nauseous or wanting to vomit. Additionally, it can describe being very tired of something or someone because you have experienced too much of them.

words.tr: phrase. 落在后面；拖在后面
words.ex: The dog trails behind when it walks slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗走得很慢时会落在后面。
words.en: To move or develop more slowly than others; to be in a position that is behind others.

words.ex: He sicken after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后生病了。
words.en: If something sickens you, it makes you feel disgusted or horrified.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.ex: The honey is sticky.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是黏的。
words.en: Something that is sticky is covered with a substance that things stick to.

words.ex: He uses chopsticks to eat rice.
words.ex_cn: 他用筷子吃米饭。
words.en: A chopstick is one of a pair of thin sticks that are used for eating, especially in East Asia.

words.ex: The book has a thick cover.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有厚厚的封面。
words.en: Having a large distance between the top and bottom or front and back surfaces; not thin.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The system has a vulnerability that hackers can exploit.
words.ex_cn: 这个系统有一个黑客可以利用的脆弱性。
words.en: The state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.

words.ex: He uses the web to find information.
words.ex_cn: 他使用网络来查找信息。
words.en: A web is a thin net made from sticky threads that a spider uses to catch insects.

words.ex: He found a weapon in the old box.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧箱子里发现了一件武器。
words.en: A weapon is an object that can be used to harm or kill someone, or to damage or destroy something.

words.ex: The clock shows accurate time.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟显示的时间很精确。
words.en: Correct in all details; exact.

words.ex: The accuracy of the clock is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟的精确性很高。
words.en: The quality or state of being correct or precise.

words.tr: adj. 不精确的；不准确的；有错误的；
words.ex: The clock is inaccurate and shows the wrong time.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟不精确，显示的时间不对。
words.en: If a statement or measurement is inaccurate, it is not correct or not exact.

words.ex: They accused him of stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他们指控他偷了钱。
words.en: If you accuse someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you say or tell them that you believe that they did it.

words.ex: He faced an accusation of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他面临偷钱的指控。
words.en: An accusation is a statement saying that someone has done something wrong or illegal.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: He wants to join the football team.
words.ex_cn: 他想加入足球队。
words.en: To become a member of a group or organization; to connect or fasten things together.

words.tr:
adj. 联合的；共同的；
n. 关节；接合处；
words.ex: They signed a joint agreement to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一项联合协议来保护环境。
words.en: A joint is a place where two things are joined together, especially the place where two bones are connected in a person's or animal's body.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.tr:
n. 硬币；金属钱币；
v. 创造；
words.ex: He has a coin in his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他口袋里有一枚硬币。
words.en: A coin is a small, flat, round piece of metal or plastic that is used as money.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

words.ex: The administration of the school is very organized.
words.ex_cn: 学校的行政管理非常有条理。
words.en: The process or activity of running a business, organization, etc., or the people who run it.

words.ex: The administrative office handles school records.
words.ex_cn: 行政办公室负责管理学校档案。
words.en: Relating to the management of a company, organization, or institution.

words.ex: The minister signed the new law.
words.ex_cn: 部长签署了新法律。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department or a member of the clergy in some Christian churches.

words.ex: The ministry of education controls schools.
words.ex_cn: 教育部管理学校。
words.en: A ministry is a government department, especially in Britain, which is responsible for a particular area of administration, such as health or education.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: She has a feminine voice.
words.ex_cn: 她的声音很女性化。
words.en: having qualities or an appearance traditionally associated with women, especially delicacy and prettiness.

words.tr: n. 女权运动；男女平等主义
words.ex: She believes in feminism and wants equal rights for women.
words.ex_cn: 她相信女权主义，希望女性享有平等权利。
words.en: Feminism is the belief and aim that women should have the same rights, power, and opportunities as men.

words.tr:
n. 女权主义者
adj. 女权主义的
words.ex: She is a feminist who believes in equal rights.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位相信平等权利的女权主义者。
words.en: A feminist is a person who believes in and supports the rights and equality of women.

words.tr:
n. 帮助；援助；
v. 帮助；协助；
words.ex: The charity provided aid to the flood victims.
words.ex_cn: 慈善机构向洪水受害者提供了帮助。
words.en: To aid someone means to help or assist them. Aid can also refer to the help or support given.

words.ex: The nurse is the doctor's aide.
words.ex_cn: 护士是医生的助手。
words.en: An aide is someone whose job is to help another person in their work.

words.ex: The maid cleans the house every morning.
words.ex_cn: 女仆每天早上打扫房子。
words.en: A maid is a woman who works as a servant in a hotel or in someone's home.

words.ex: It was her maiden flight on a plane.
words.ex_cn: 这是她第一次坐飞机。
words.en: A maiden is a young girl or woman who is not married.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.ex: The factory will automate the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将自动化装配线。
words.en: To automate a factory, office, or industrial process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

words.ex: The factory uses automation to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用自动化来制造汽车。
words.en: The use of largely automatic equipment in a system of manufacturing or other production process.

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.ex: He drives an automobile to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A vehicle that is powered by an engine and is used for carrying passengers on roads.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.tr: phrase. 磁条卡；带有磁性条纹的塑料卡片（用于存储数据，常见于银行卡、门禁卡等）
words.ex: He swiped his magstripe card to pay for the groceries.
words.ex_cn: 他用磁条卡支付了杂货。
words.en: A magstripe card is a type of card capable of storing data by modifying the magnetism of tiny iron-based magnetic particles on a band of magnetic material on the card.

words.ex: The conversion of water into steam takes heat.
words.ex_cn: 水变成蒸汽需要热量。
words.en: The process of changing or causing something to change from one form to another.

words.ex: He drives a red convertible on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末开一辆红色敞篷车。
words.en: A convertible is a car with a roof that can be folded down or removed.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: The inverse order of the numbers is 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的倒序是5、4、3、2、1。
words.en: If there is an inverse relationship between two things, one of them becomes larger as the other becomes smaller.

words.ex: The inversion of the matrix is difficult.
words.ex_cn: 矩阵的逆矩阵很难求。
words.en: An inversion is a change in the position, order, or relationship of things so that they are the opposite of what they were before.

words.ex: The speed is inversely proportional to the time.
words.ex_cn: 速度与时间成反比。
words.en: In an inverse manner; in the opposite order, direction, or effect.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.ex: The tree grows in a vertical line.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树垂直生长。
words.en: Something that is vertical stands or points straight up.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The company will advertise its new phone on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司将在电视上为新手机登广告。
words.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

words.ex: He saw an advertisement on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他在电视上看到一则广告。
words.en: An advertisement is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event or publicizing a job vacancy.

words.tr: n. 广告活动；广告业； v. 做广告；“advertise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company launched a new advertising campaign last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月推出了一项新的广告活动。
words.en: The activity of producing advertisements for commercial products or services.

words.tr: n. 少许；小块；片刻； v. “bite”的过去式；
words.ex: Can you give me a bit of sugar?
words.ex_cn: 你能给我一点点糖吗？
words.en: A bit is a small piece or quantity of something.

words.tr:
n. 咬；咬伤；上钩；
v. 咬；叮；上钩；
words.ex: The dog gave him a sudden bite.
words.ex_cn: 狗突然咬了他一口。
words.en: If an animal or person bites you, they use their teeth to cut into your flesh.

words.tr: adj. 有苦味的；激烈而不快的；痛苦的；刺痛的；
words.ex: The medicine tastes bitter.
words.ex_cn: 这种药尝起来很苦。
words.en: Having a sharp, pungent taste or smell; not sweet. Feeling or showing anger, hurt, or resentment because of bad experiences or a sense of unjust treatment.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.ex: The children left litter on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在海滩上留下了垃圾。
words.en: If a place is littered with something, it contains many examples of it that are usually not arranged neatly or properly.

words.ex: You won't pass the test unless you study.
words.ex_cn: 除非你学习，否则你不会通过考试。
words.en: You use unless to introduce the only circumstances in which an event you are mentioning will not take place or in which a statement you are making is not true.

words.ex: She blesses her children every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上为孩子们祝福。
words.en: If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.

words.tr: n. 幸事； v. “bless”的现在分词；
words.ex: Finding a good job after graduation was a blessing.
words.ex_cn: 毕业后找到一份好工作是一件幸事。
words.en: A blessing is a prayer asking for God's favor and protection, or a beneficial thing for which one is grateful.

words.tr:
adj. 幸福的；受祝福的；神圣的
v. 祝福；保佑；“bless”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She is blessed with a kind heart.
words.ex_cn: 她拥有一颗善良的心。
words.en: Made holy; consecrated.

words.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨了；尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Despite what has just been said or done; nonetheless.

words.ex: It was raining, nonetheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下着雨，尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Nonetheless is used to indicate that something is true or happens in spite of what has just been said.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 史诗的；叙事诗的；宏丽的；
words.ex: The movie tells an epic story of heroes and dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影讲述了一个关于英雄和龙的史诗故事。
words.en: An epic is a long book, poem, or film, whose story extends over a long period of time or tells of great events.

words.ex: The Industrial Revolution was a new epoch in history.
words.ex_cn: 工业革命是历史上一个新时代。
words.en: An epoch is a period of time in history or a person's life, typically one marked by notable events or particular characteristics.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.tr:
n. 岩石；摇滚乐；
v. （使）摇动；（使）摇晃；
words.ex: The children climbed on the big rock near the river.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在河边的大岩石上攀爬。
words.en: A rock is a large piece of stone that forms part of a hill or mountain. Rock can also refer to a type of music that is loud and has a strong beat. As a verb, to rock means to move gently backwards and forwards or from side to side.

words.ex: The rocky path made hiking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 多岩石的小路让徒步变得困难。
words.en: A rocky area is covered with rocks or consists of large areas of rock and has nothing growing on it.

words.ex: The ship arrived at the dock at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 船在日出时到达了码头。
words.en: A dock is an enclosed area of water in a port where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.

words.ex: He forgot the keys to the locks.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了锁的钥匙。
words.en: Locks are devices used to secure doors, containers, etc., and can also refer to sections of a canal or river where the water level changes, controlled by gates.

words.tr: n. （有锁的）寄物柜；锁柜；上锁的人
words.ex: He put his books in the locker.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放在储物柜里。
words.en: A locker is a small storage compartment, typically in a public place such as a school, gym, or workplace, where individuals can store their personal belongings securely.

words.ex: The two teams are in a deadlock over the budget.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队在预算上陷入了僵局。
words.en: A deadlock is a situation in which no progress can be made or no agreement is reached, especially because of a disagreement between two or more parties.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.ex: The two countries are in the same bloc.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家属于同一个集团。
words.en: A bloc is a group of countries or parties with similar political interests, especially when they act together in international affairs.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.tr:
adv. 顺时针方向地
adj. 顺时针方向的
words.ex: Turn the knob clockwise to open the jar.
words.ex_cn: 顺时针转动旋钮来打开罐子。
words.en: Moving in the same direction as the hands of a clock.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.tr:
n. 震惊；冲击；电击；震动；
v. 使震惊；使震动；
words.ex: The news of his death was a shock to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他去世的消息让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: A shock is a sudden, unexpected event or piece of news that causes a strong emotional reaction.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.ex: We walked along the coast and saw the sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们沿着海岸散步，看到了大海。
words.en: The coast is the land along the edge of the sea or ocean.

words.ex: The coastal village has beautiful beaches.
words.ex_cn: 这个沿海村庄有美丽的海滩。
words.en: relating to the coast, the area where the land meets the sea

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 自吹自擂的；自夸的
words.ex: He is boastful about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他炫耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone is boastful, they talk too proudly about something that they have done or that they own.

words.tr:
n. 烤肉；烘烤；
adj. 烤的；焙的；
v. 烤；烘烤；
words.ex: We had roast for dinner last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚我们吃了烤肉。
words.en: To cook food, such as meat, in an oven or over a fire.

words.ex: She ate a slice of toast for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 她早餐吃了一片烤面包。
words.en: Toast is bread which has been cut into slices and made brown and crisp by cooking at a high temperature. Toast is also a drink in which you wish someone happiness or success.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.ex: He excels in math.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长数学。
words.en: To be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject.

words.tr: adj. 优秀的；杰出的；卓越的；
words.ex: He got an excellent score on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中取得了优异的成绩。
words.en: Something that is excellent is very good indeed.

words.ex: He showed excellence in math competitions.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中表现出色。
words.en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

words.ex: He picked up the parcel from the post office.
words.ex_cn: 他从邮局取了包裹。
words.en: A parcel is something wrapped in paper, usually so that it can be sent to someone by post.

words.tr:
n. 傻瓜；蠢人；
v. 愚弄；
words.ex: He is a fool for spending all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他是个傻瓜，把所有钱都花在游戏上了。
words.en: A fool is someone who behaves in a silly way without thinking or someone who is tricked into believing or doing something that is not sensible.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.tr:
n. 人们；人民；
adj. 民间的；
words.ex: The folk in the village are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 村子里的人们非常友好。
words.en: Folk can refer to people in general, or to a particular group of people. It can also refer to traditional music or customs of a community.

words.tr: n. 民间传说；民俗学；民间风俗；
words.ex: The old man told us a folklore about a dragon living in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 老人给我们讲了一个关于住在山里的龙的民间传说。
words.en: Folklore is the traditional stories, customs, and habits of a particular community or nation.

words.ex: I forget where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you forget something, you fail to remember it.

words.ex: He is forgetful and often loses his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他很健忘，经常丢钥匙。
words.en: Someone who is forgetful often forgets things.

words.ex: The movie was forgettable and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影容易被忘，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as forgettable, you mean that they do not have any qualities that make them special, unusual, or interesting.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.tr: n. 伪造；伪造罪；伪造物
words.ex: He was arrested for forgery.
words.ex_cn: 他因伪造被逮捕了。
words.en: Forgery is the crime of making or altering a document or signature with the intent to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: I forgive you for being late.
words.ex_cn: 我原谅你迟到了。
words.en: If you forgive someone who has done something bad or wrong, you stop being angry with them and stop blaming them.

words.tr:
adj. 宽恕的；宽大的；仁慈的
v. 原谅；宽恕；“forgive”的现在分词
words.ex: She is a forgiving person who forgets mistakes easily.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个宽恕的人，容易忘记错误。
words.en: If you describe someone as forgiving, you mean that they are kind and tolerant towards someone who has hurt them or done something wrong.

words.ex: The hikers walked through a deep gorge.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走过一个深峡谷。
words.en: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, often carved by a river. It can also refer to the act of eating greedily.

words.ex: She wore a gorgeous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件华丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you say that something is gorgeous, you mean that it gives you a lot of pleasure or is very attractive.

words.tr:
v. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；抨击；达到；
n. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；(演出等)成功；
words.ex: He hit the ball with a bat.
words.ex_cn: 他用球棒打了球。
words.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

words.ex: He is a man of great wit.
words.ex_cn: 他是个极具机智的人。
words.en: Wit is the ability to use words or ideas in a quick, clever, and amusing way.

words.ex: He gave a witty answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题给出了机智的回答。
words.en: Someone or something that is witty is amusing in a clever way.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.tr:
n. 荣誉；荣幸；尊敬；
v. 尊敬；给予荣誉；履行；
words.ex: He received an honor for his brave actions.
words.ex_cn: 他因勇敢的行为获得了荣誉。
words.en: Honor is a quality that combines respect, pride, and honesty. A person who has honor is someone who is admired and respected because of his or her integrity and ethical behavior.

words.tr: adj. 光荣的；可敬的；尊敬的
words.ex: He is an honorable man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是说真话的正直的人。
words.en: Deserving respect and admiration; having high moral standards.

words.tr: adj. 荣誉的；名誉的；道义上的
words.ex: He received an honorary degree for his work.
words.ex_cn: 他因自己的工作获得了荣誉学位。
words.en: Given as an honor without the usual requirements or duties.

words.tr:
n. 主人；主持人；
v. 主持；
words.ex: The host welcomed us with tea and cookies.
words.ex_cn: 主人用茶和饼干欢迎了我们。
words.en: A host is a person who receives or entertains guests, especially in their own home. A host is also a person who presents a television or radio program.

words.tr: n. 女主人；女房东；女招待；女主持人；
words.ex: The hostess welcomed us with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 女主人微笑着欢迎我们。
words.en: A woman who receives or entertains guests in a social or official capacity; a woman who is in charge of a particular event or place and who welcomes and looks after the people who attend.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.ex: He went to the hospital because he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感觉不舒服去了医院。
words.en: A hospital is a place where people who are ill or injured are treated and taken care of by doctors and nurses.

words.tr: v. 送医院治疗；使住院
words.ex: He was hospitalized after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后被送进了医院。
words.en: To admit someone into a hospital for treatment.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.ex: The host showed great hospitality to the guests.
words.ex_cn: 主人对客人表现出极大的款待。
words.en: Hospitality is friendly and generous behaviour towards guests, especially by giving them food, drink, or a place to stay.

words.ex: The robbers took a hostage during the bank robbery.
words.ex_cn: 劫匪在银行抢劫时抓了一名人质。
words.en: A hostage is someone who has been captured by a person or organization and who may be killed or injured if people do not do what that person or organization demands.

words.ex: The children said they saw a ghost in the old house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们说他们在老房子里看到了一个鬼。
words.en: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person that some people believe they can see or feel.

words.ex: His humor makes everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他的幽默让大家都笑了。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comic, especially as expressed in literature or speech.

words.ex: He tells humorous stories that make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲一些幽默的故事，让大家都笑。
words.en: If you are humorous, you are able to be amusing and to make people laugh.

words.ex: The doctor found a tumor in his lung.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的肺里发现了一个肿瘤。
words.en: A tumor is a mass of tissue that's formed by an accumulation of abnormal cells. Normally, the cells in your body age, die, and are replaced by new cells. With cancer and other tumors, something disrupts this cycle. Tumor cells grow, even though the body does not need them, and unlike normal old cells, they don't die. As this process goes on, the tumor continues to grow as more and more cells are added to the mass.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.tr:
n. 功能；职责；
v. 起作用；
words.ex: The function of this button is to turn on the light.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮的功能是打开灯。
words.en: A function is the purpose that something is designed to have or the job that someone is employed to do. It can also refer to a mathematical relationship or a social event.

words.tr: adj. 功能的；起作用的；实用的；
words.ex: This chair is functional and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子功能性强且舒适。
words.en: Relating to the way in which something works or operates.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: He loves reading science fiction.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读科幻小说。
words.en: Fiction refers to literature in the form of prose, especially novels, that describes imaginary events and people.

words.ex: The story is fictional and not based on real events.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是虚构的，不是基于真实事件。
words.en: Fictional refers to something that is invented or imagined, and not necessarily based on real events or people.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: n. 避难所；庇护所；庇护；
words.ex: The birds found sanctuary in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟在森林里找到了避难所。
