words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.tr: n. 扭曲；歪曲；失真；畸变；
words.ex: The photo showed distortion in the lines.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中的线条出现了扭曲。
words.en: A distortion is a change, twist, or exaggeration that makes something appear different from the way it really is.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr:
v. 中止；中断；放弃；堕（胎）
n. 中止计划
words.ex: He decided to abort the mission because it was too dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 他决定中止任务，因为太危险了。
words.en: If an unborn baby is aborted, the pregnancy is ended deliberately and the baby is not born alive.

words.ex: She decided to have an abortion.
words.ex_cn: 她决定进行流产。
words.en: An abortion is a medical procedure to end a pregnancy so it does not result in the birth of a baby.

words.ex: He walked forth to meet the sun.
words.ex_cn: 他向前走去迎接太阳。
words.en: Forward in time, place, or order; onward.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.ex: He made a gamble on the horse race.
words.ex_cn: 他在这场赛马上赌了一把。
words.en: If you gamble on something, you take a risky action or decision in the hope of gaining something.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.tr: v. 萦绕；“haunt”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The memory of his mistake still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 他错误的回忆仍然萦绕着他。
words.en: If a place is haunted, it is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.tr: adj. 萦绕心头的；使人难忘的； v. “haunt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The haunting melody stayed in my mind all day.
words.ex_cn: 那萦绕心头的旋律在我脑海中盘旋了一整天。
words.en: Something that is haunting is so beautiful or sad that it stays in your thoughts for a long time.

words.ex: He wore a weird hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶怪异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as weird, you mean that they are strange, unusual, or mysterious.

words.tr: pron. 他们的；她们的；它们的；
words.ex: Their books are on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他们的书在桌子上。
words.en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.

words.ex: The heiress inherited a large fortune from her grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 这位女继承人从她祖父那里继承了一大笔财富。
words.en: A woman who is legally entitled to inherit property or a title from someone who has died.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.ex: The lobbyist talked to the senator about the new law.
words.ex_cn: 游说者向参议员谈论了这项新法律。
words.en: A lobbyist is a person who tries to influence legislation on behalf of a special interest; a member of a lobby.

words.tr: phrase. 屈服于；向…让步；投降
words.ex: Don't give in to fear when you face a challenge.
words.ex_cn: 当你面对挑战时，不要向恐惧屈服。
words.en: To yield to someone or something, especially after resisting for a period of time.

words.ex: He reads books as a hobby.
words.ex_cn: 他读书作为一种爱好。
words.en: A hobby is an activity that you enjoy doing in your spare time.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.ex: The line is horizontal on the graph.
words.ex_cn: 这条线在图上是水平的。
words.en: Parallel to the plane of the horizon; at right angles to the vertical.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The lamp provides illumination in the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯为黑暗的房间提供照明。
words.en: The act of providing or casting light on something, or the state of being lit up; also, the clarification or elucidation of a subject or issue.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.ex: The luminous moon lights up the night.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的月亮照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is luminous shines or glows in the dark.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: phrase. 远非；远不及；完全不；差得远
words.ex: The movie was nowhere near as good as the book.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影远不及书好。
words.en: not nearly; not at all

words.ex: The mountain has great prominence in the landscape.
words.ex_cn: 这座山在景观中十分突出。
words.en: If someone or something is in a position of prominence, they are important or well-known.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.ex: He is a man of great eminence in science.
words.ex_cn: 他在科学界享有很高的声望。
words.en: Eminence refers to a position of great distinction or superiority, especially in a particular field or profession.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: The country practiced imperialism in the 1800s.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在19世纪实行帝国主义。
words.en: Imperialism is a policy or ideology of extending a country's rule over foreign nations, often by military force or by gaining political and economic control of other areas.

words.tr:
n. 帝国主义者
adj. 帝国主义的
words.ex: The imperialist country took over many colonies.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国主义国家占领了许多殖民地。
words.en: An imperialist is a person who supports or practices imperialism, which is a policy of extending a country's power and influence through colonization, use of military force, or other means.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: He got a driver's license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A license is an official document which gives you permission to do, use, or own something.

words.ex: The forest is dense with trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林树木茂密。
words.en: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

words.ex: The density of water is 1 gram per cubic centimeter.
words.ex_cn: 水的密度是每立方厘米1克。
words.en: Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.

words.ex: The steam condenses into water when it touches the cold glass.
words.ex_cn: 当蒸汽接触到冷的玻璃时，会凝结成水。
words.en: If you condense something, especially a piece of writing or a speech, you make it shorter, usually by including only the most important parts.

words.ex: The condensation of the report made it easier to read.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告的浓缩版更容易阅读。
words.en: Condensation is the process by which a gas changes into a liquid, or the liquid that results from this process.

words.tr:
n. 负荷；载重；
v. 载入；
words.ex: The bridge can't hold such a heavy load.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥承受不了这么重的负荷。
words.en: A load is a large quantity of something that is carried by a vehicle, person, or animal, or the amount of work that a person or machine has to do.

words.ex: He will upload his homework tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚会上传他的作业。
words.en: To transfer data or files from a local computer to a remote computer or server.

words.ex: I download music from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 我从互联网下载音乐。
words.en: To download data means to transfer it to your computer or device from another computer or from the internet.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.tr: adj. 修辞性的；词藻华丽的；反问的
words.ex: He asked a rhetorical question to make a point.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个修辞性的问题来阐明观点。
words.en: A rhetorical question is one which is asked in order to make a statement rather than to get an answer.

words.tr:
n. 抒情诗；歌词
adj. 抒情的
words.ex: He wrote a lyric about the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于日落的抒情诗。
words.en: Lyric refers to the words of a song, especially a popular song, or to a short poem that expresses personal feelings and thoughts.

words.tr: adj. 抒情诗般的；充满感情的；热情奔放的
words.ex: He sings a lyrical song about the sea.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一首关于大海的抒情歌曲。
words.en: Lyrical means expressing the writer's emotions in an imaginative and beautiful way.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He took a remedial math course to improve his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一门补救数学课程来提高自己的技能。
words.en: Remedial actions or activities are intended to correct something that is wrong or to improve a bad situation.

words.ex: The baby smiled at the sweet melody.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝听到了甜美的旋律，笑了。
words.en: A melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodious song at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时唱出旋律优美的歌。
words.en: If something such as a voice or a tune is melodious, it is pleasant to listen to because it has a musical quality.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.ex: The train went through a long tunnel.
words.ex_cn: 火车通过了一条长长的隧道。
words.en: A tunnel is a long passage which has been made under or through the ground, usually through a hill or under a river, to allow people or vehicles to travel through it.

words.tr: n. 专家咨询组；嵌板；仪器板；
words.ex: The government formed a panel to advise on health policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府组建了一个专家咨询组来就卫生政策提供建议。
words.en: A panel is a small group of people who are chosen to do something, for example to discuss something in public or to make a decision.

words.ex: They found paradise on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个小岛上找到了天堂。
words.en: Paradise is a place of ideal beauty or loveliness, or a state of supreme happiness.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；
v. 分阶段进行；
words.ex: The project is in its final phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正处于最后阶段。
words.en: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.

words.ex: He learned a new phrase in Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他学了一个新的西班牙语短语。
words.en: A phrase is a short group of words that people often use as a way of saying something. The meaning of a phrase is often not obvious from the meaning of the individual words in it.

words.ex: He learned many phrasal verbs in English class.
words.ex_cn: 他在英语课上学到了许多短语动词。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of a phrase or phrases.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.tr:
n. 控制；管制；
v. 控制；操纵；
words.ex: The teacher has good control of the class.
words.ex_cn: 老师对课堂有很好的控制。
words.en: To control something means to have power over it and to be able to make it do what you want.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.tr:
v. 引用；报价；
n. 引用；引文；报价；
words.ex: He quoted Shakespeare in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中引用了莎士比亚的话。
words.en: To repeat or copy out (a group of words from a text or speech), typically with an indication that one is not the original author or speaker.

words.ex: He asked for a quotation for the new computer.
words.ex_cn: 他询问了新电脑的报价。
words.en: A quotation is a sentence or phrase taken from a book, poem, play, etc., which is repeated by someone else, or a statement of the current price of something.

words.ex: The factory has a quota of 1000 units per day.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂每天有1000件的配额。
words.en: A quota is the limited number or quantity of something which is officially allowed.

words.ex: He lost his wallet on the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他在公交车上丢了钱包。
words.en: A wallet is a small flat folding case made of leather or plastic, in which you can keep banknotes, credit cards, and other small flat objects.

words.ex: The soldier picked up a bullet from the ground.
words.ex_cn: 士兵从地上捡起一颗子弹。
words.en: A bullet is a small piece of metal with a pointed or rounded end, which is fired from a gun.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.tr: n. 平板电脑；（刻有文字的）匾；
words.ex: He uses a tablet to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他用平板电脑读书。
words.en: A tablet is a small, flat computer that is controlled by touching the screen. It can also refer to a small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: Please stir the soup before serving.
words.ex_cn: 请在上菜前搅拌一下汤。
words.en: To mix a substance or move it around using a spoon or other object; to cause to move or act; to arouse or excite.

words.tr:
v. （使）回旋；（使）旋转
n. 一连串的事；混乱；尝试
words.ex: The wind makes the leaves whirl around.
words.ex_cn: 风让树叶旋转飞舞。
words.en: To move or cause to move rapidly around and around.

words.ex: Ancient warfare used swords and shields.
words.ex_cn: 古代战争使用剑和盾。
words.en: Warfare is the activity of fighting a war.

words.ex: The warrior fought bravely to protect his village.
words.ex_cn: 这位战士勇敢地战斗以保护他的村庄。
words.en: A warrior is a person who is engaged in or experienced in battle, or who shows or has shown great vigor, courage, or aggressiveness, as in politics or athletics.

words.ex: The evidence warrants a new investigation.
words.ex_cn: 证据使新的调查成为必要。
words.en: If something warrants a particular action, it makes the action seem necessary or appropriate for the circumstances.

words.tr: n. 保证；保修单；保证书
words.ex: The phone comes with a one-year warranty.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一年的保修期。
words.en: A warranty is a written guarantee, often given to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.ex: The bird flew aloft above the trees.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在树顶上方高飞。
words.en: If something is aloft, it is in the air or off the ground.

words.ex: The police found a clue at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了一条线索。
words.en: A clue is an object or piece of information that helps to solve a problem or mystery.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.tr:
n. 长队；
v. 排队；
words.ex: There is a long queue at the ticket counter.
words.ex_cn: 售票处排着一条长队。
words.en: A queue is a line of people or vehicles waiting for something.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: He showed indulgence when his son stayed out late.
words.ex_cn: 当他儿子深夜外出时，他表现出了纵容。
words.en: If you have an indulgence, you allow yourself to have or do something that you enjoy, especially something that is considered bad for you.

words.tr: adj. 纵容的；宽厚的；溺爱的
words.ex: Her parents are indulgent and let her stay up late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很纵容，让她熬夜。
words.en: If you are indulgent, you treat someone with special kindness, often in a way that is not good for them.

words.tr: n. 噩梦；不愉快的经历；
words.ex: He had a nightmare about falling from a tall building.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个从高楼坠落的噩梦。
words.en: A nightmare is a very frightening dream.

words.ex: He visits his grandparents every fortnight.
words.ex_cn: 他每两周拜访一次祖父母。
words.en: A fortnight is a period of two weeks.

words.tr:
adv. 在夜里；突然；
adj. 整晚的；
words.ex: The baby slept overnight in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿整夜睡在小床上。
words.en: If something happens overnight, it happens during the night or for the period of one night. It can also mean happening very quickly or suddenly.

words.ex: The knight rode a horse and wore shiny armor.
words.ex_cn: 骑士骑着马，穿着闪亮的盔甲。
words.en: In the Middle Ages, a knight was a man of high social rank who had a duty to fight for his king. Knights are often depicted as noble warriors on horseback.

words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.ex: The child was restless during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在漫长的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If you are restless, you are unable to stay still or to be calm and happy, because you are bored or worried.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: Her beloved dog always greeted her at the door.
words.ex_cn: 她钟爱的狗总是在门口迎接她。
words.en: Dearly loved.

words.ex: He shoved his way through the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他挤过人群。
words.en: To push someone or something in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: He cooks soup on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 他用炉子煮汤。
words.en: A stove is a piece of equipment which provides heat, either for cooking or for heating a room.

words.tr:
n. 鸽子；鸽派人物；温和派人物
v. 潜水；跳水；“dive”的过去式
words.ex: The dove flew over the garden.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子飞过花园。
words.en: A dove is a bird that is often used as a symbol of peace. It is known for its gentle nature and the soft cooing sound it makes.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.tr: adj. 有节奏的；有韵律的；
words.ex: The children danced to the rhythmic beat.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们随着有节奏的节拍跳舞。
words.en: A rhythmic sound or movement has a clear and regular pattern that is repeated.

words.tr: n. 头痛；令人头痛的人（或事物）；
words.ex: He got a headache after working too long.
words.ex_cn: 他工作太长时间后得了头痛。
words.en: A headache is a pain in your head. If you say that something is a headache, you mean that it causes you difficulty or worry.

words.tr:
n. 疼痛；隐痛；渴望
v. 疼痛；隐痛
words.ex: My head aches after staying up late.
words.ex_cn: 我熬夜后头痛。
words.en: If you ache or a part of your body aches, you feel a steady, fairly strong pain.

words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

words.ex: The proximate cause of the accident was bad weather.
words.ex_cn: 事故的直接原因是恶劣天气。
words.en: If something is proximate, it is nearest in space, time, or relationship.

words.ex: The proximity of the school to the park makes it nice for kids.
words.ex_cn: 学校靠近公园，对孩子们来说很好。
words.en: Proximity refers to the state of being near in space or time.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.ex: The approximation of pi is 3.14.
words.ex_cn: π的近似值是3.14。
words.en: An approximation is a fact, object, or description which is similar to something else, but which is not exactly the same.

words.ex: The trip takes approximately 30 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 这段旅程大约需要30分钟。
words.en: Used to indicate that something is close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact.

words.tr: n. 织物；（建筑物的）结构；
words.ex: The dress is made of soft fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子是由柔软的织物制成的。
words.en: Fabric refers to cloth or other material produced by weaving together cotton, nylon, wool, silk, or other threads. It can also refer to the basic structure of a building or a system.

words.ex: He fabricates excuses to avoid work.
words.ex_cn: 他编造借口来逃避工作。
words.en: To fabricate means to invent or produce something false in order to deceive someone.

words.ex: The fabrication of the machine took three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的制备花了三周时间。
words.en: The act of inventing or producing something false in order to deceive someone.

words.tr:
n. 浸泡；
v. 吸收；
words.ex: The clothes went into a soak overnight.
words.ex_cn: 衣服泡了一整晚。
words.en: To soak something means to make it very wet by leaving it in a liquid, or to become very wet in this way. It can also mean to absorb or take in something.

words.ex: The oak tree stands tall in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 栎树矗立在后院。
words.en: An oak is a large tree that is common in northern countries. Oaks have strong wood and are often used for making furniture.

words.tr:
n. 斗篷；掩护物
v. 隐瞒；掩饰
words.ex: He wore a black cloak to hide his face.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件黑色斗篷来遮住脸。
words.en: A cloak is a long, loose outer garment which is worn over other clothes, especially in cold weather. It can also refer to something that hides or covers another thing.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: He gave an arrogant answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: Someone who is arrogant behaves in a proud, unpleasant way towards other people because they believe that they are more important than others.

words.ex: His arrogance made others dislike him.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让其他人不喜欢他。
words.en: Arrogance is the quality of being arrogant, which means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities.

words.ex: She wore an elegant dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条优雅的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe a person or thing as elegant, you mean that they are pleasing and graceful in appearance or style.

words.ex: Her dress showed great elegance.
words.ex_cn: 她的裙子展现了极大的优雅。
words.en: Elegance is the quality of being graceful and stylish in appearance or manner.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: The plane began its descent at 10,000 feet.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在一万英尺高度开始下降。
words.en: The act of moving or falling downward.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: n. 香味；香水；气息；察觉；
words.ex: The flower has a sweet scent.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有甜美的香味。
words.en: A scent is a pleasant smell, especially one that is characteristic of a particular thing. It can also refer to the ability to detect smells or a clue or indication of something.

words.ex: He earned a bachelor in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了计算机科学学士学位。
words.en: A bachelor is a man who has never been married.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr:
v. 重新洗牌；改组
n. 改组；重新安排
words.ex: The coach will reshuffle the team for the next game.
words.ex_cn: 教练将为下一场比赛重新调整阵容。
words.en: to change the positions of people or things within a group, especially in order to improve the way it works

words.ex: The smoke began to stifle her breathing.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾开始让她窒息。
words.en: To stifle something means to prevent it from happening, continuing, or developing.

words.tr:
n. 琐事；少量
v. 玩弄；轻视
words.ex: He threw away a trifle of money on candy.
words.ex_cn: 他花了一点钱买糖果。
words.en: A trifle is something that is considered to have little importance, value, or significance. It can also refer to a small amount of something. As a verb, to trifle means to treat someone or something without seriousness or respect.

words.ex: She practices ballet every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 她每天下午练习芭蕾舞。
words.en: Ballet is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the 15th century and later developed into a concert dance form in France and Russia. It has since become a widespread, highly technical form of dance with its own vocabulary based on French terminology. It has been globally influential and has defined the foundational techniques used in many other dance genres.

words.tr: adj. 秃头的；不加修饰的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The old man is bald.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是秃头的。
words.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

words.ex: The herald announced the king's arrival.
words.ex_cn: 传令官宣布了国王的到来。
words.en: A herald is someone who carries or proclaims important news; a forerunner or harbinger.

words.tr:
n. 坟墓；
adj. 严重的；
words.ex: They visited the grave of their grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他们参观了祖父的坟墓。
words.en: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried. When used as an adjective, grave means serious or solemn.

words.ex: The gravity of Earth pulls objects down.
words.ex_cn: 地球的重力把物体往下拉。
words.en: Gravity is the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth or towards any other physical body having mass.

words.ex: The apple fell because of gravitation.
words.ex_cn: 苹果掉下来是因为重力。
words.en: Gravitation is the force of attraction that exists between any two masses, any two bodies, any two particles. It is the force that pulls objects towards each other.

words.ex: The brave firefighter saved the child from the fire.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从火中救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is brave is willing to do things which are dangerous, and does not show fear in difficult or dangerous situations.

words.ex: His bravery saved the children from the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他的勇敢救了孩子们于火海之中。
words.en: Bravery is the quality of being brave; courage.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.ex: A gentle breeze blew through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一阵微风轻轻吹过树梢。
words.en: A breeze is a gentle wind.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.ex: The birds sing at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时歌唱。
words.en: The first appearance of light in the sky before sunrise; the beginning of a phenomenon or period of time.

words.tr:
v. 打呵欠
n. 呵欠
words.ex: He yawned during the boring lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的讲座上打哈欠。
words.en: If you yawn, you open your mouth very wide and breathe in more air than usual, often because you are tired or bored.

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.ex: Water evaporation happens when the sun heats the lake.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳加热湖泊时，水就会蒸发。
words.en: Evaporation is the process by which a liquid turns into a gas.

words.ex: The water vapor rose into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 水蒸气升上了天空。
words.en: Vapor is a substance in the gas phase at a temperature lower than its critical temperature, which means that the vapor can be condensed to a liquid by increasing its pressure without reducing the temperature.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲；曲线；
v. （使）弯成弧形；
words.ex: The road has a sharp curve ahead.
words.ex_cn: 前面的路有一个急转弯。
words.en: A curve is a smooth, gradually bending line, for example part of the edge of a circle.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.tr: v. 繁荣兴旺；茁壮成长；
words.ex: The business flourishes in the new market.
words.ex_cn: 这家企业在新市场中繁荣兴旺。
words.en: If something flourishes, it is successful, active, or common, and developing quickly and strongly.

words.ex: Mother's milk nourishes the baby.
words.ex_cn: 母乳滋养婴儿。
words.en: To nourish someone or something means to provide them with the food and other substances they need in order to live, grow, and be healthy.

words.ex: Milk provides good nourishment for children.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶为儿童提供良好的滋养品。
words.en: Nourishment refers to the food or other substances necessary for growth, health, and good condition.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.tr: adj. 易腐烂的；易坏的；易毁灭的
words.ex: Milk is a perishable food.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶是一种易腐食品。
words.en: Likely to decay or go bad quickly.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.ex: He takes the metro to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天乘地铁去上班。
words.en: A metro is an underground railway system in a city.

words.tr: adj. 大都市的；大城市的；
words.ex: He lives in a metropolitan city like New York.
words.ex_cn: 他住在纽约这样的大都市。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a metropolis or large city, especially as the main city of a country or region.

words.ex: The firefighter is a hero for saving the child.
words.ex_cn: 消防员救了孩子，是个英雄。
words.en: A hero is a person who is admired for their courage, outstanding achievements, or noble qualities.

words.ex: The heroine saves the town from the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 女主角拯救了小镇免受龙的侵害。
words.en: A heroine is a woman who is admired for her courage, outstanding achievements, or noble qualities, especially a woman who has performed a heroic act or is the main character in a story.

words.ex: The heroic firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位英勇的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: If you describe a person or their actions as heroic, you admire them because they show extreme bravery.

words.tr: n. 英雄表现；英雄气概
words.ex: His heroism saved many lives during the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他的英勇行为在火灾中救了许多人的生命。
words.en: Heroism is great bravery, especially in a difficult situation or in a war.

words.ex: She picked up a needle to sew the button.
words.ex_cn: 她拿起一根针来缝纽扣。
words.en: A needle is a thin, pointed piece of metal that is used in sewing. It has a hole at one end for thread to pass through.

words.ex: The baby was sleeping in the cradle.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在吊架里睡觉。
words.en: A cradle is a small bed for a baby, which can be rocked from side to side. It can also refer to the place or period in which something begins or is developed.

words.tr:
v. 挤作一团
n. 挤作一团
words.ex: The team huddled together to plan their next move.
words.ex_cn: 团队聚在一起规划下一步行动。
words.en: If people huddle together, they stand, sit, or lie close to each other because they are cold or frightened.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.tr: v. 兜售；沿街叫卖； 散播
words.ex: He tries to peddle fake watches on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在街上兜售假手表。
words.en: To peddle goods or ideas means to try to sell them or make them accepted by going from place to place.

words.ex: He pressed the pedal to speed up the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下踏板让自行车加速。
words.en: A pedal is a lever that you press with your foot in order to control a vehicle or machine.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.tr:
n. 马鞍；鞍座
v. 给（马）装鞍
words.ex: The boy rode on a saddle on the horse.
words.ex_cn: 男孩骑在马的马鞍上。
words.en: A saddle is a seat for a rider on the back of a horse or other animal, or a similar seat on a bicycle or motorcycle. It can also refer to the act of putting a saddle on a horse or to burden someone with a responsibility.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.ex: The car moved rapidly down the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车迅速地沿着道路行驶。
words.en: If something happens rapidly, it happens very quickly.

words.ex: He looks up to his favorite singer as an idol.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己最喜欢的歌手当作偶像。
words.en: An idol is a person or thing that is greatly admired, loved, or revered.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.ex: He used an idiomatic expression in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个惯用表达。
words.en: If you refer to someone's idiomatic use of a language, you mean that they use it in a way that sounds natural and correct to native speakers of that language.

words.ex: He called his friend an idiot after the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他在犯错后称朋友是白痴。
words.en: An idiot is a person who is considered to be very stupid or foolish.

words.ex: His idiotic comments made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那些愚蠢的评论让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you call someone or something idiotic, you mean that they are very stupid or silly.

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: The augmentation of data helps the model learn better.
words.ex_cn: 数据的增加帮助模型学得更好。
words.en: The act or process of making or becoming greater in size or amount.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: The inauguration of the new bridge was celebrated with a parade.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的落成典礼以一场游行来庆祝。
words.en: The act of starting a new operation or practice; the formal admission of someone to office.

words.tr: n. 测量仪器；规格；评估；
words.ex: The mechanic used a gauge to check the tire pressure.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用一个测量仪器来检查轮胎气压。
words.en: A gauge is a device that measures the amount or quantity of something and shows the measurement in a form that is easy to read, such as a dial or a digital display.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.tr: adj. 惹人生气的； v. “irritate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is irritating.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很惹人生气。
words.en: If you describe something as irritating, you mean that it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr: n. 搅动；煽动；激动；不安
words.ex: The agitation of the water made the dirt rise.
words.ex_cn: 水的搅动使灰尘浮起。
words.en: Agitation is a state of anxiety or nervous excitement.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.ex: He spoke without hesitation.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不犹豫地说了。
words.en: Hesitation is the act of pausing before doing something, especially because you are nervous or not certain about it.

words.ex: He was hesitant to answer the question.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着不敢回答这个问题。
words.en: If you are hesitant about doing something, you are slow to do it, usually because you are uncertain, worried, or nervous about it.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

words.ex: He ate a chunk of cheese for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一大块奶酪。
words.en: A chunk of something is a large piece or amount of it.

words.tr: v. 喝；喝酒；“drink”的过去分词； adj. 喝醉的；
words.ex: He has drunk all the water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了所有的水。
words.en: If someone is drunk, they have consumed so much alcohol that it has affected their ability to think and speak clearly.

words.ex: The drunken man stumbled down the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个醉汉摇摇晃晃地走在街上。
words.en: Someone who is drunken is drunk or frequently gets drunk.

words.tr: n. 树干；大衣箱；象鼻子；
words.ex: The elephant held the branch with its trunk.
words.ex_cn: 大象用它的鼻子抓住树枝。
words.en: The main stem of a tree, below the branches, and above the ground; the main part of the body, excluding the head, arms, and legs; the long, flexible nose of an elephant; a large, strong box used for transporting or storing clothes and other personal possessions.

words.ex: The company has a simple logo on its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的产品上有一个简单的标志。
words.en: A logo is a design or symbol used by a company to identify its products, services, or itself.

words.ex: The ship carries a large cargo of rice.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船运载了大量大米货物。
words.en: Cargo refers to the goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or other large vehicle.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈悲的；宽大的
words.ex: The judge was merciful and gave him a small fine.
words.ex_cn: 法官很仁慈，只判了他一笔小额罚款。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as merciful, you mean that they show or have mercy.

words.tr: adj. 残忍的；无情的；无慈悲心的；
words.ex: The merciless storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场残忍的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe someone as merciless, you mean that they are very cruel or determined and do not show any concern for the effect their actions have on other people.

words.ex: The murder happened last night in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这起谋杀发生在昨晚的公园里。
words.en: Murder is the unlawful premeditated killing of one human being by another.

words.ex: The murderous storm killed many people.
words.ex_cn: 这场致命的风暴夺去了许多人的生命。
words.en: If you describe an action or a way of behaving as murderous, you mean that it is very violent and intended to kill someone.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.ex: He kept neutrality during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: The state of not supporting or helping either side in a conflict, disagreement, etc.; impartiality.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a small dose of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一小剂量的药。
words.en: A dose of a medicine or a drug is the amount of it that you take at one time, or the amount that is recommended for you to take.

words.ex: The doctor adjusted the dosage of the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生调整了药物的剂量。
words.en: The amount of a medicine or drug that is taken at one time or over a period of time.

words.ex: He dozed off during the boring meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在无聊的会议上打起了瞌睡。
words.en: To doze means to sleep lightly or for a short period.

words.ex: I bought a dozen eggs from the store.
words.ex_cn: 我从商店买了十二个鸡蛋。
words.en: If you have a dozen things, you have twelve of them.

words.ex: He has a big nose.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个大鼻子。
words.en: The part of the face or head that contains the nostrils and organs of smell and through which a person or animal breathes.

words.tr: adj. 爱管闲事的；爱打听的
words.ex: The nosy neighbor always asks too many questions.
words.ex_cn: 那个爱管闲事的邻居总是问太多问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as nosy, you mean that they are too interested in things that do not concern them, especially other people's affairs.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: He writes simple prose every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写简单的散文。
words.en: Prose is written language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.ex: The intrusion of strangers made her feel unsafe.
words.ex_cn: 陌生人的闯入让她感到不安全。
words.en: An intrusion is an unwanted event or person in a situation where they are not welcome or do not belong.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: He was rude to the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务员很无礼。
words.en: If someone is rude, they behave in a way that is not polite and upsets other people.

words.tr:
adj. 裸体的
n. 裸体；裸体画；裸体像
words.ex: He painted a nude woman by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一位在窗边的裸体女性。
words.en: A nude person is not wearing any clothes. A nude painting or sculpture shows a person who is not wearing any clothes.

words.ex: The movie shows nudity in one scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影在一个场景中展示了裸体。
words.en: The state or fact of being naked.

words.tr:
adj. 平静的；镇静的；
v. （使）平静；（使）镇定；
n. 平静；
words.ex: The lake was calm in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很平静。
words.en: If someone is calm, they are not excited, anxious, or upset, but are rational and composed.

words.ex: The palm tree grows near the beach.
words.ex_cn: 棕榈树长在海滩附近。
words.en: The inner surface of the hand that extends from the wrist to the base of the fingers; also refers to the tropical tree with large divided leaves.

words.tr: adj. 严厉的；严峻的；冷酷无情的；坚定的；可怕的
words.ex: He had a grim look on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严峻的表情。
words.en: If a situation or piece of news is grim, it is very serious, unpleasant, and depressing.

words.ex: The pilgrim walked to the holy place.
words.ex_cn: 朝圣者步行前往圣地。
words.en: A pilgrim is a person who journeys to a sacred place for religious reasons.

words.tr: n. 朝圣之旅；参拜之行；瞻仰之旅；
words.ex: Many people go on a pilgrimage to the holy city.
words.ex_cn: 许多人前往圣城进行朝圣之旅。
words.en: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place for religious reasons.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr: adj. 苗条的；纤细的；微小的；
words.ex: She has a slim figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: If someone is slim, they are thin in an attractive way.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.tr: n. 公共卫生；卫生设施；
words.ex: The city improved sanitation to keep people healthy.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市改善了公共卫生以保障人民健康。
words.en: The conditions and processes that help maintain health and prevent disease, especially through cleanliness.

words.ex: The kitchen must be sanitary to prevent illness.
words.ex_cn: 厨房必须保持清洁以防止疾病。
words.en: relating to the conditions that affect hygiene and health, especially the supply of sewage facilities and clean drinking water

words.ex: The ball is a perfect sphere.
words.ex_cn: 这个球是一个完美的球体。
words.en: A sphere is a perfectly round three-dimensional shape, like a ball. It can also refer to a particular area of interest, activity, or knowledge.

words.ex: The ball is spherical.
words.ex_cn: 这个球是球状的。
words.en: Something that is spherical is round like a ball.

words.ex: The atmosphere keeps the Earth warm.
words.ex_cn: 大气使地球保持温暖。
words.en: The atmosphere is the layer of gases surrounding a planet or other material body, held in place by the gravity of the body.

words.ex: The atmospheric pressure dropped before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴来临前，大气压下降了。
words.en: Relating to the atmosphere of the Earth or another planet; creating a distinctive mood, typically of romance or nostalgia.

words.ex: The Earth is divided into two hemispheres: north and south.
words.ex_cn: 地球被分为两个半球：北半球和南半球。
words.en: A hemisphere is one half of the earth, especially the northern or southern half above or below the equator, or the eastern or western half.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.tr: phrase. 放置一旁；留出；不理会；取消
words.ex: He sets aside $50 each week for savings.
words.ex_cn: 他每周存下50美元作为储蓄。
words.en: To reserve or keep something for a particular purpose or person.

words.ex: The two countries argued over territorial rights.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家就领土权利发生了争执。
words.en: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea.

words.ex: The concert was terrific!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something or someone as terrific, you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

words.tr:
n. 曲调；调子；
v. 调整；调音；
words.ex: He hummed a happy tune while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时哼着一首欢快的曲调。
words.en: A tune is a series of musical notes that are pleasant to listen to. It can also refer to adjusting something so that it works or looks better.

words.tr: n. [英]地铁；管子；管状物；电视机；
words.ex: I take the tube to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上乘地铁去上班。
words.en: A tube is a long, hollow cylinder used for conveying or holding liquids or gases.

words.ex: He poured water into the tub.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进了桶里。
words.en: A tub is a large, open container that you fill with water and use to wash yourself or to wash clothes.

words.ex: We took the ferry to cross the river.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘渡船过河。
words.en: A ferry is a boat that transports passengers and sometimes also vehicles, usually across rivers or short stretches of sea.

words.ex: He picked a red berry from the bush.
words.ex_cn: 他从灌木丛中摘了一颗红色浆果。
words.en: A berry is a small, round fruit that grows on a bush or a tree. Some berries are edible and can be eaten raw or used in cooking.

words.ex: The children are merry on Christmas day.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节那天很开心。
words.en: If you describe someone's character or behavior as merry, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.ex: The children laughed with merriment at the circus.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在马戏团里开心地大笑。
words.en: Merriment is the quality or state of being merry, characterized by joy and laughter.

words.ex: The Gulf of Mexico is a large sea area.
words.ex_cn: 墨西哥湾是一个大型海域。
words.en: A gulf is a large area of sea that is partly surrounded by land.

words.ex: I will borrow a book from the library.
words.ex_cn: 我将从图书馆借一本书。
words.en: To take and use something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: He wiped the sweat from his brow.
words.ex_cn: 他擦去了额头上的汗水。
words.en: The brow refers to the eyebrow or the forehead, and can also denote the top edge of a steep place such as a cliff.

words.ex: He raised his eyebrow when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时抬起了眉毛。
words.en: An eyebrow is the line of hair that grows above your eye.

words.ex: I like to browse the internet for fun.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢上网浏览消遣。
words.en: To look through or glance at reading matter casually or randomly.

words.ex: He uses Chrome as his browser.
words.ex_cn: 他用 Chrome 作为他的浏览器。
words.en: A browser is a piece of computer software that you use to search for information on the Internet.

words.tr: n. 马达；发动机；机动车；
words.ex: The car has a strong motor.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个强大的马达。
words.en: A motor is a device that changes energy into mechanical motion, especially such a device that provides power for a vehicle or for another device with moving parts.

words.ex: They stayed at a motel near the highway.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在高速公路旁的一家汽车旅馆。
words.en: A motel is a hotel which is designed for people who are travelling by car, usually with parking spaces next to each room.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.ex: The clown amuses the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: If something amuses you, it makes you want to laugh or smile.

words.tr: adj. 逗人笑的； v. “amuse”的现在分词；
words.ex: The clown gave an amusing performance.
words.ex_cn: 小丑的表演很逗人笑。
words.en: Something that is amusing makes you laugh or smile.

words.ex: Children find amusement in playing games.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在玩游戏时感到快乐。
words.en: Amusement is the feeling that you have when you think that something is funny or entertaining.

words.tr:
n. 脏乱；杂乱；
v. 弄糟；
words.ex: The room was a mess after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A mess is a situation that is confused and full of problems, or something that is dirty or untidy.

words.ex: His room is messy with clothes everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间很杂乱，衣服到处都是。
words.en: If you describe something as messy, you mean that it is untidy or dirty.

words.ex: He sent a message through a messenger.
words.ex_cn: 他通过信使发送了一条消息。
words.en: A messenger is someone who carries messages from one person to another.

words.ex: He gave his mother a massage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后给妈妈做了按摩。
words.en: The act of rubbing and pressing someone's body with the hands to reduce tension or pain in the muscles.

words.tr:
v. 屠杀 
n. 大屠杀
words.ex: The soldiers committed a massacre in the village.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里进行了大屠杀。
words.en: The indiscriminate killing of a large number of people.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.ex: The beast ran fast through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 那只野兽在森林里快速奔跑。
words.en: A beast is a large and dangerous animal.

words.ex: The mother fed her baby with her breast.
words.ex_cn: 母亲用乳房喂养她的婴儿。
words.en: The front part of a person's body between the neck and the stomach, or the similar part on a bird or animal.

words.ex: They walked abreast down the street.
words.ex_cn: 他们并肩走在街上。
words.en: If people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, side by side, and often facing the same direction.

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

words.tr: n. （身体或精神的）极度痛苦
words.ex: He felt deep anguish after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他感到极度痛苦。
words.en: Anguish is extreme mental suffering or physical pain.

words.tr: adv. 无论什么；任何(用于否定句中以加强语气)；
words.ex: You can eat whatever food whatsoever.
words.ex_cn: 你可以吃任何食物。
words.en: used to emphasize a negative statement

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: My ancestor came from China a hundred years ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先一百年前来自中国。
words.en: An ancestor is a person from whom one is descended, typically more remote than a grandparent.

words.ex: He learned about his ancestry from his grandmother.
words.ex_cn: 他从祖母那里了解了自己的血统。
words.en: Your ancestry is the series of ancestors from whom you are descended.

words.ex: He told an anecdote about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的趣事。
words.en: An anecdote is a short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident or person.

words.ex: His argument is based on anecdotal evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点基于轶事证据。
words.en: Anecdotal evidence is based on personal accounts rather than on research that can be verified.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.ex: He must face up to his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的错误。
words.en: If you face up to a difficult situation, you accept it and deal with it honestly and bravely.

words.tr:
v. 交叠；使部分重叠；
n. 重叠部分；
words.ex: The two colors overlap on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 两种颜色在墙上交叠。
words.en: If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing. You can also say that two things overlap.

words.tr:
v. 鼓掌；拍手
n. 鼓掌；拍手
words.ex: The crowd will clap after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众会鼓掌。
words.en: To clap means to strike the palms of your hands together to show appreciation or to make a noise.

words.tr:
n. 钩；扣；紧握；紧抱
v. 抱紧；握紧；扣紧
words.ex: The necklace has a gold clasp.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链有一个金色的钩。
words.en: A clasp is a small device that fastens something, or the act of holding someone or something tightly.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.tr:
v. 拍；掴；拍击
n. 拍；掴；拍击
words.ex: He slapped the table in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地拍了桌子。
words.en: If you slap someone, you hit them with the palm of your hand.

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: His speech was coherent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲连贯且易于理解。
words.en: If something is coherent, it is well planned, so that it is clear and sensible and all its parts go well with each other.

words.ex: The story has good coherence, so it is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事很有连贯性，所以很容易理解。
words.en: Coherence is the quality of being logical and consistent.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: The adherence of the sticker to the wall is strong.
words.ex_cn: 贴纸对墙的粘附很强。
words.en: Adherence is the act of following or sticking to a particular set of beliefs, principles, or rules.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.ex: The numbers show convergence over time.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字随时间显示出收敛。
words.en: The process or state of converging; the coming together of two or more things to a common point or conclusion.

words.tr: v. 报（某事）之仇；为（某人）报仇
words.ex: He wants to avenge his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为弟弟的死报仇。
words.en: To avenge someone means to harm or punish someone who has harmed them or someone they care about.

words.tr:
n. 报复；报仇
v. 报复
words.ex: He wanted revenge for his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为他兄弟的死报仇。
words.en: Revenge involves hurting or punishing someone who has hurt or harmed you.

words.tr: adj. 深藏仇恨的；燃起复仇念头的
words.ex: He was revengeful after being betrayed by his friend.
words.ex_cn: 被朋友背叛后，他心怀仇恨。
words.en: If you describe someone as revengeful, you mean that they are eager to seek revenge.

words.ex: He wanted vengeance after his brother was hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他哥哥被伤害后，他想要报复。
words.en: Vengeance is the act of doing something harmful or unpleasant to someone because they have done something harmful or unpleasant to you.

words.ex: The school forbids students to use phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: To forbid something means to order that it must not be done.

words.tr: adj. 禁止的；不许的； v. “forbid”的过去分词；
words.ex: The forbidden area is off-limits to visitors.
words.ex_cn: 这个禁止区域对游客关闭。
words.en: If something is forbidden, you are not allowed to do it or have it.

words.tr:
n. 努力争取；出价；投标；
v. 出价；投标；
words.ex: His bid for the championship inspired everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他为冠军所做的努力鼓舞了所有人。
words.en: To bid means to offer a particular amount of money for something that is being sold, especially at an auction, or to offer to do work or provide services for a particular price.

words.tr:
n. 轨道；
v. 绕...轨道而行；
words.ex: The moon moves around the Earth in an orbit.
words.ex_cn: 月亮围绕地球在轨道上运行。
words.en: An orbit is the curved path, usually elliptical, described by a planet, satellite, spaceship, etc., around a celestial body, as the sun.

words.ex: The satellite moves in an orbital path around Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星在围绕地球的轨道上运行。
words.en: Relating to an orbit or orbits.

words.tr: adj. 眶下的；亚轨道的；不满轨道一整圈的
words.ex: The suborbital flight lasted only a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 亚轨道飞行只持续了几分钟。
words.en: Relating to or being a trajectory that does not complete a full orbit around the Earth or another celestial body.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.ex: The archer drew the bow and shot the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 弓箭手拉弓射出了箭。
words.en: A bow is a knot with two loops and two loose ends that is used in tying shoelaces and decorative ribbons. It is also the front part of a ship or boat.

words.tr:
n. 肘部
v. 用肘推挤
words.ex: He hurt his elbow while playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他在打篮球时伤了肘部。
words.en: The joint between the forearm and the upper arm; to push someone with your elbow.

words.ex: The rainbow appears after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后出现了彩虹。
words.en: A rainbow is an arch of different colors that appears in the sky when the sun shines through rain.

words.ex: He ate soup from a bowl.
words.ex_cn: 他从碗里吃汤。
words.en: A bowl is a round container with a wide uncovered top. Some kinds of bowl are used, for example, for serving or eating food from, or in cooking, while other larger kinds are often used for washing or other purposes.

words.ex: The tree has many branches.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树有许多分支。
words.en: A branch of a tree is one of its parts that grows out from its trunk. A branch of a business or organization is one of its offices or shops that are in different places.

words.ex: He works on a large ranch in Texas.
words.ex_cn: 他在德克萨斯州的一个大牧场工作。
words.en: A ranch is a large farm, especially in the western United States and Canada, where cattle or other animals are bred and raised.

words.ex: He bought a franchise to open a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一个特许经营权来开一家咖啡店。
words.en: A franchise is an authorization granted by a government or company to an individual or group enabling them to carry out specified commercial activities, e.g., acting as an agent for a company's products.

words.ex: He eats fiber to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃纤维来保持健康。
words.en: A fiber is a thread or a structure or object resembling a thread, especially one that is used to make cloth or rope.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: He went to jail for bribery.
words.ex_cn: 他因贿赂而入狱。
words.en: Bribery is the act of offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting something of value for the purpose of influencing the action of an official in the discharge of his or her public or legal duties.

words.ex: The tribe lives in the forest and follows old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在森林里，遵循古老的传统。
words.en: A tribe is a social division in a traditional society consisting of families or communities linked by social, economic, religious, or blood ties, with a common culture and dialect, typically having a recognized leader.

words.ex: The tribal people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 部落的人住在森林里。
words.en: Tribal relates to a tribe or tribes.

words.ex: The dog ran through the mud.
words.ex_cn: 狗跑过了泥地。
words.en: Mud is a sticky mixture of earth and water.

words.tr: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的；
words.ex: The road became muddy after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，这条路变得泥泞。
words.en: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud or full of mud. If you muddy something, you make it muddy or you make it less clear or more complicated.

words.ex: The trees bud in spring.
words.ex_cn: 树木在春天发芽。
words.en: A bud is a small pointed lump that appears on a tree or plant and develops into a leaf or flower.

words.ex: I went to the park with my buddy.
words.ex_cn: 我和我的同伴去了公园。
words.en: A buddy is a close friend.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.ex: There is a vacancy in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 销售部门有一个空缺职位。
words.en: A vacancy is a position or job that is available for someone to fill.

words.ex: The volcano erupted last year.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山去年喷发了。
words.en: A volcano is a mountain that opens downward to a pool of molten rock below the surface of the earth. When pressure builds up, eruptions occur.

words.ex: The volcanic eruption destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷发摧毁了村庄。
words.en: Volcanic is used to describe things that are connected with volcanoes or caused by volcanoes.

words.ex: He paddles a canoe on the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他划着独木舟在湖上航行。
words.en: A canoe is a small, narrow boat that you move through the water using a paddle.

words.ex: The clan lived in a small village for centuries.
words.ex_cn: 这个氏族几个世纪以来一直住在一个小村庄里。
words.en: A clan is a group of families or relatives who are connected by blood or marriage and who often share the same surname.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；攫住
n. 紧抓；离合器；一窝雏；一小群；紧要关头
words.ex: He clutched the rope tightly when he slipped.
words.ex_cn: 当他滑倒时，他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To clutch something means to hold it tightly, usually because you are afraid or anxious. In a vehicle, the clutch is a pedal that you press with your foot to change gears.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: The workers dug a trench to lay the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 工人们挖了一条沟来铺设管道。
words.en: A trench is a long, narrow ditch. In warfare, trenches are dug by troops to provide shelter from enemy fire.

words.ex: He sat on the bench in the park.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在公园的长凳上。
words.en: A bench is a long seat for several people, typically made of wood or metal.

words.tr:
v. 握紧；捏紧；咬牙切齿
n. 抓紧；咬紧；抓紧用具
words.ex: He clenched his fist when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时握紧了拳头。
words.en: To close or hold something very tightly, especially in a determined or angry way.

words.tr:
v. 猛扭；扭伤；挣脱
n. 扳手；扳钳；（离别的）痛苦
words.ex: He wrenched the door open with all his strength.
words.ex_cn: 他用尽全力猛扭门，把它打开了。
words.en: A wrench is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, pipes, etc. It can also refer to a sudden violent twist or pull, or a feeling of sadness or distress caused by separation.

words.ex: She uses cosmetic cream to make her skin look better.
words.ex_cn: 她使用美容霜让皮肤看起来更好。
words.en: A cosmetic is a substance that you put on your face or body to improve its appearance.

words.ex: The comet shines brightly in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 彗星在夜空中明亮地闪耀。
words.en: A comet is a celestial object consisting of a nucleus of ice and dust and, when near the sun, a 'tail' of gas and dust particles pointing away from the sun.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr:
n. 誓言；誓约
v. 发誓；起誓
words.ex: He made a vow to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓戒烟。
words.en: A vow is a serious promise or decision to do something.

words.tr:
v. 修剪；扫杀
n. 麦秆堆；干草堆积处
words.ex: He mows the lawn every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期六都割草。
words.en: To cut down (grass or grain) with a scythe or a machine.

words.ex: He uses a mower to cut the grass.
words.ex_cn: 他用割草机割草。
words.en: A mower is a machine for cutting grass or other plants that grow on the ground.

words.tr:
v. 牵引；拖
n. 牵引；拖
words.ex: He tows his broken car to the garage.
words.ex_cn: 他把坏掉的车拖到修理厂。
words.en: To pull a vehicle or boat along behind another vehicle, using a rope or chain.

words.ex: He dried his hands with a towel.
words.ex_cn: 他用毛巾擦干手。
words.en: A towel is a piece of thick soft cloth that you use to dry yourself with.

words.ex: He grabbed the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速抓住了球。
words.en: If you grab something, you take it or pick it up suddenly and roughly.

words.tr:
n. 刺；戳
v. 刺；戳
words.ex: He felt a sharp stab in his side.
words.ex_cn: 他感到侧腹一阵刺痛。
words.en: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

words.tr:
n. 乘船游览；航游；
v. 乘船游览；航游；
words.ex: We went on a cruise around the Mediterranean Sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘船游览了地中海。
words.en: To sail about in an area without a precise destination, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: The cruiser sailed slowly across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 巡洋舰缓缓驶过海洋。
words.en: A cruiser is a large fast warship, or a large motorboat used for pleasure trips.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.ex: He reads scripture every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读经文。
words.en: The sacred writings of a religion; often used to refer to the Bible.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.ex: I asked the school for a transcript of my grades.
words.ex_cn: 我向学校要了一份成绩单的副本。
words.en: A transcript is a written or printed version of something that has been recorded or spoken, especially in the context of academic records.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.ex: The movie's depiction of ancient life is very realistic.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对古代生活的描写非常真实。
words.en: A depiction of something is a picture or a written description of it.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.ex: He washed his hands to remove the dirt.
words.ex_cn: 他洗手以去除污垢。
words.en: Dirt is any substance that makes something unclean, such as mud or dust.

words.ex: The floor is dirty after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 下雨后，地板变得肮脏了。
words.en: If something is dirty, it is marked or covered with stains, spots, or mud, and needs to be cleaned.

words.tr:
v. 调情；轻率地对待
n. 与多人调情的人
words.ex: He flirts with her at the coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡店向她调情。
words.en: If you flirt with someone, you behave as if you are sexually attracted to them, in a playful or not very serious way.

words.tr: n. 调情；挑逗；逢场作戏
words.ex: She dismissed the flirtation as just a harmless game.
words.ex_cn: 她将这次调情视为一场无伤大雅的游戏。
words.en: Flirtation is behavior that suggests a sexual attraction to someone but is not meant to be taken seriously.

words.tr: n. 管道工程； v. “plumb”的现在分词；
words.ex: He works as a plumber and fixes plumbing in houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名水管工，负责修理房屋的管道工程。
words.en: The system of pipes, tanks, fittings, and other apparatus required for the water supply, heating, and sanitation in a building.

words.ex: The plumber fixed the leaky pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水管工修好了漏水的管道。
words.en: A plumber is a person whose job is to connect and repair things such as water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets.

words.ex: He gave a dumb answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个愚笨的回答。
words.en: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak. If you describe someone or something as dumb, you mean that they are stupid or silly.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
